And I am not in this war for Dooku's politics. I am the leader of the most powerful droid army the galaxy has ever seen.''"
"''An army with no loyalty, no spirit, just programming. What have you to show for all your power? What have you to gain?"
"The future! A future where there are no Jedi.|Grievous and Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=GrievousMotivation.flac|{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}}} '''Grievous''', [[Reproduction|born]] '''Qymaen jai Sheelal''', was a [[Kaleesh]] [[Gender|male]] [[warlord]] who served within the [[Confederacy military|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] as a [[commanding officer]] during the [[Clone Wars]] in the final [[Standard year|year]]s of the [[Republic Era]]. In addition to his position as a [[general]] within the [[Separatist Droid Army]], the Kaleesh held the title of [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies]] throughout the war, where he led countless engagements against the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic|Grand Army]]. Recognized for his ruthless tactics and extensive [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] enhancements, Grievous utilized the Separatist [[Droid]] [[Army]] and his adept combat skills to instill fear throughout [[the galaxy]] as he traveled to and invaded [[planet]]s while engaging numerous [[Jedi Knight|Knights]] of the [[Jedi Order]], his sworn enemies. A [[Homeworld|native]] of [[Kalee]], a planet within [[Wild Space]], Sheelal grew to become a fearsome [[Soldier|warrior]] of his people and gained an aptitude for warfare and battle tactics when he led his people during Kaleesh's [[Kaleesh-Yam'rii war|war]] against the [[Yam'rii]], their technologically advanced adversary and planetary neighbor, an [[insect]]oid species invading from the desolate planet [[Huk]] in the system of the [[Huk system|same name]] near [[Kalee system|their own]]. Qymean jai Sheelal eventually took the name "Grievous" and became a feared warlord on his homeworld, earning a [[blood]]y reputation. Gathering together, Grievous traveled and fought alongside his personal [[bodyguard]]s, the [[Izvoshra]]. The [[Sith Lord]]s [[Darth Sidious]] and [[Darth]] [[Dooku|Tyranus]]—also known as Dooku, the [[Count of Serenno|Count]] of [[Serenno]]—recognized Grievous' potential when he led his people in a merciless war against the Yam'rii and successfully drove them from their world, then launched a series of devastating campaigns on Huk itself, sweeping across the Huk worlds. However, the [[Galactic Republic]] and [[Jedi]] Order intervened in the conflict on the side of the Yam'rii, leading to punishment and famine for the Kaleesh and generating an enduring grudge in Grievous. The Sith, who had significant plans for Grievous, offered Grievous cybernetic enhancements, which the Kaleesh accepted and took on over [[time]]. Sometime later, Dooku conspired to mortally wound Grievous and [[Sabotage of Grievous' shuttle|sabotaged]] his [[Grievous' shuttle|shuttle]], which resulted in a gruesome crash that left the man on the brink of [[death]]. After that, Grievous gave up almost everything that remained of his organic form—whether lost in the crash or by his own decision-making—to survive. The reconstructed Grievous became a skilled [[lightsaber duel]]ist under Dooku's guidance, who trained the Kaleesh in the arts of [[lightsaber combat]] and eventually welcomed him into a position as a warrior in the Confederacy. Shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis|advent]] of the Clone Wars, Grievous was quickly granted the rank of general, as well as the title of Supreme Martial [[Commander]] of the Separatist Droid Armies, making him one of the most powerful people within the Separatist Alliance, second only to his master Dooku. Grievous wielded his skills as a brilliant military strategist and melee combatant during numerous campaigns against the Republic throughout the Clone Wars while also gaining a reputation for [[hunt]]ing and killing Jedi Knights as a [[Jedi hunter]]. He made a habit of claiming the [[lightsaber]]s of defeated Jedi as trophies and [[weapon]]s to be used against other opponents. His position and threat level led to his preeminence as one of the Republic's primary targets throughout the course of the war. As the war played out, Grievous found a personal nemesis in [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], whom he dueled on numerous occasions. [[Standard day|Days]] before the end of the war in [[19 BBY]], Grievous, under orders from Darth Sidious, launched a daring and unprecedented [[Battle of Coruscant|assault]] on the planet [[Coruscant]], the [[capital]] world of the Republic. In his assault, the Kaleesh managed to take the Republic's [[Supreme Chancellor]], Sheev Palpatine—in reality secretly Sidious himself—captive aboard his [[flagship]], the [[Providence-class Dreadnought|''Providence''-class Dreadnought]] ''[[Invisible Hand]]''. However, during the battle, the Chancellor was rescued from the general's grasp by [[Jedi General]]s Obi-Wan Kenobi and [[Anakin Skywalker]], an engagement that also resulted in Dooku's death. Subsequently, Grievous became the de facto leader of the entire Separatist Alliance and immediately withdrew of all remaining reinforcements and fled into the [[Outer Rim Territories]], prolonging the war. Following the Battle of Coruscant, Grievous, succeeding Dooku as the Confederacy's Head of State, retreated to the planet [[Utapau]], where he addressed and relocated the members of the Executive Separatist Council to the planet [[Mustafar]] under Sidious's orders. However, unknown to the general, Grievous's location on Utapau was betrayed by Sidious, resulting in a Republic [[Battle of Utapau|invasion]] of the planet in an effort to bring a decisive conclusion to the war. Grievous was ultimately slain by his nemesis, General Kenobi, following a prolonged chase between the two, which resulted in the war's conclusion as well as the Confederacy's systematic collapse soon after. ==Biography== ====Early life==== =====Warlord of Kalee===== {{Quote|Although perhaps not obvious at first glance, one of the most well-known (certainly most notorious) Kaleesh was General Grievous, the feared warrior who was so instrumental for the Separatists during the Clone Wars.|An artist's journal, on Grievous' origins|}} Qymaen jai Sheelal, the [[Kaleesh]] [[Gender|male]] who would eventually become "Grievous," was [[Reproduction|born]] into his [[Grievous's family|family]] [[Standard year|years]] prior to the [[Clone Wars]], [[Homeworld|hailing]] from[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens Beginner Game|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' Beginner Game]] the wilderness''[[Hyperspace Stories: Grievous]]'' of the [[Wild Space]] [[planet]] [[Kalee]]. Sheelal was born in the midst of an [[Kaleesh-Yam'rii war|almost continual war]] between the Kaleesh and their planetary neighbor,{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} (Spanish version) the [[Yam'rii]], an [[insect|insectoid]] [[species]]{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} from the desolate planet{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|55|History of the Ship}} (English version) [[Huk]]''[[Rise of the Separatists]]'' in the [[Huk system]]{{GalaxyMapAppendix}} next to [[Kalee system|Kalee's own]]. Though the Yam'rii inflicted great damage upon Sheelal's people, the Kaleesh retained their zeal for conquering other societies during the conflict, and since [[Youngling|childhood]], Sheelal worshipped the [[warlord]]s of Kalee as he watched them return home with spoils of war from those they conquered.''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' [[File:Kaleesh-Alien_Archive.jpg|thumb|left|240x240px|A Kaleesh warrior.]] Sheelal was taught how to use a [[slugthrower]],{{EncyclopediaCite|The Separatists}} (English version) the [[Czerka Arms]] [[Outland rifle]], by his [[Grievous's father|father]]. By the age of eight he served as a [[sniper]] and had already [[Death|killed]] forty enemies. As he matured, Sheelal experienced a rapid rise in [[Military rank|rank]], becoming a feared [[Soldier|warrior]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' and warlord.''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' He learnt brutal and determined strategy, battle tactics, and warfare in the war against the Yam'rii. Becoming a successful warlord of Kalee with numerous enemies, Sheelal bore an exceptional{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|45|History of the Ship}} capacity to instruct, encourage, and manage his fellow [[Kaleesh warrior]]s excellently. Amongst Kaleesh warriors, he donned his [[Kaleesh mask|fearsome masks]]. One was carved from the [[Bone|skull]], bone, and [[Tooth|teeth]]{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} (Spanish version) of his [[homeworld]]'s deadliest [[Diet|predatory]] beast, the [[mumuu]], while another was carved from the bones of an [[erkush]].{{GEAttr|Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities}} Before going into battle,''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]'' his [[Grievous's masks|customary mask]] was smeared with patterns of [[karabbac]]-[[blood]] warpaint. Like members of his species, known for his lack of mercy''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' and an obsession with the glory gathered in war, he valued bravery in combat above all else throughout his life and started his [[Collector|collection]] of [[weapon]]s as trophies. Sheelal became one of the greatest military leaders, a proud,{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}} honorable, and revered warrior,''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]'' and the Kaleesh grew to regard him as a legendary figure. At that [[time]], Sheelal also began to develop a deep hatred for the [[Galactic Republic]]. He was further frustrated by the realization that the [[Jedi Knight]]s of the [[Jedi Order]], the protectors of the Republic,{{Film|II}} were nearly undefeatable in close combat through their possession of [[Force power|supernatural abilities]] originating from a mystical energy field known as [[the Force]].{{Film|IV}} He despised the Jedi for their skill. Sheelal had earned a bloody reputation as a powerful warlord of his homeworld and eventually adopted the moniker "Grievous,"{{EncyclopediaCite|Battle Droids and Other Droids of War}} whose name inspired fear in the hearts of his enemies. Over his [[Standard year|years]] of battle, Grievous traveled and battled alongside Kalee's best warriors, the [[Izvoshra]]. He would assemble them into his elite{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|55|History of the Ship}} [[bodyguard]]s, with each a [[khan]] in command of troops of their own. Seemingly always alongside their warlord leader, the courageous Izvoshra shared in his victories and love of battle alike.{{BuildR2Cite|57|Droid Directory}} Fortunately for Grievous, his reputation had drawn the attention of the [[Sith]]—[[Dooku|Darth Tyranus]], also known as [[Count]] Dooku, who discovered Grievous{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Sith Information Guide|cardname=General Grievous|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022691/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith-37-S-General-Grievous}} for the Sith, and his [[Sith Master]], [[Darth Sidious]], secretly the Republic [[Politics|politician]] Sheev Palpatine—who saw his potential as he led his people in a ruthless battle against their technologically superior enemies, the Yam'rii. Legend claimed that they specifically were interested in his strength, power, and will to succeed.{{StoryCite|story=The Droid with a Heart|book=Myths & Fables}} The Sith had been recruiting minions who possessed unique skills and a deep hatred of the Jedi, both of which Grievous had in abundance. As per the plan for the [[Cloning|Clone]] Wars, the Sith needed to recruit someone to lead a droid [[army]].''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' In particular, Grievous's hatred for the Jedi pushed him to near-madness and made him easily exploitable. =====Beyond Kalee===== {{Quote|I have toppled nations, I have slain kings, I have murdered legends!|Grievous on his several victories|audio=IHaveToppleNationsIHaveSlainKingsIHaveMurderLegends-BFII.flac|}} [[File:Pre-robo_grievous.png|thumb|right|295x295px|A statue of Grievous holding an enemy's severed head, a member of the Skrilling species.]] Accompanied by his Izvoshra, Grievous turned his attention to the [[star]]s to continue his conquests. Over the course of his exploits, Grievous came to topple nations, slay [[king]]s, and murder legends. At some point, he encountered a [[Wookiee warrior]]''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' and decapitated a member of the [[Skrilling]] species. Grievous then went to war against the Yam'rii with increased vigor and determination while on the offensive. In time, the Kaleesh forces successfully drove the Yam'rii from their world. Grievous launched a series of devastating campaigns on Huk itself, sweeping across the Huk worlds, where he relied on the help of his bodyguards. However, the Yam'rii took an unexpected turn and sought assistance from the Republic. The Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order intervened, siding with the Yam'rii against the invaders. The Kaleesh faced punishment; embargos and penalties were enforced, resulting in hundreds of thousands of deaths from starvation. At the time, Grievous's hatred only deepened, and he developed a personal vendetta against the Republic and the Jedi for their assistance to the Yam'rii. After their catastrophic intervention, he swore to exact terrible vengeance against the Republic and the Jedi for his people's suffering. Perhaps due to that animosity, Grievous decided to associate with the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]] and joined its ranks as an [[Enforcer (occupation)|enforcer]]. However, when he demanded that his loyal Izvoshra remain by his side, the request was denied, and he was forbidden from continuing to utilize their services. Instead, Grievous was assigned leadership of the IGBC's [[droid]] army, which he despised. After requesting a more [[Sentience|intelligent]] personal guard and consulting with Count Dooku, [[Holowan Laboratories]]' [[engineer]]s were then authorized to construct a specific series of droids to fulfill Grievous's exacting standards. Thus, the [[IG-100 MagnaGuard|IG-100 series MagnaGuard]] [[Battle droid|combat droids]], or the prototype of autonomous combat with heuristic programming, were created. At the time of their creation, various fighting techniques were implanted in their memory, but Grievous insisted on having them erased of all knowledge{{HelmetCollectionCite|24|Helmets}} so that he could train them himself. He ordered and made certain that the MagnaGuards who served under him were outfitted with [[cloak]]s and half-hoods from his homeworld, in honor of his original faithful Izvoshra bodyguards, as well as an homage to the traditions worn on his homeworld. Grievous was tremendously successful, making him one of the IGBC's more vulnerable resources. By this time, not only Count Dooku but Darth Sidious himself had already taken notice of his exploits and had important intentions for him. =====Becoming a cyborg===== {{Quote|Sometimes I wonder why you submitted to the changes.''"
"''Improvements! I submit to no one! I chose them!|EV-A4-D and Grievous|audio=ISubmitToNoOne-LoG.flac|}} [[File:Sidious_Tyranus.png|thumb|left|295x295px|Count Dooku and his Sith Master, Darth Sidious.]] Grievous chose to become a [[cyborg]], receiving his enhancements over time, after the Sith gave him an unquestionable chance. They had been looking to test technologically advanced beings, and Grievous agreed to take on the tests. On Dooku's invitation, the Kaleesh fighter sacrificed practically all of his physical body to increase his skills, strength, and speed in combat to even rival a [[Jedi Master]]{{BuildXWingCite|47|Starfighter Aces}} through extreme cybernetic upgrades to make himself an even more threatening and powerful warrior.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' These augmentations turned an already capable warrior into a nearly unstoppable killing machine on the battlefield, giving him capabilities beyond those of a normal soldier. His transformation occurred over a period of time; Grievous gradually traded many of his biological parts for upgraded mechanical ones to become a murderous cyborg with one obsession: killing Jedi. By the time of his choice, Grievous had grown psychotic and thus saw his enhancements as a logical development. With his living Kaleesh flesh traded for cyborg implants, Grievous claimed that his changes were improvements he chose to celebrate. As recounted in one legend, Grievous's transformation had been over time, he initially only made simple enhancements before moving on to more extreme changes. The legend said Grievous transformed himself because he admired the logic of droids and wanted to mirror their infallibility, strength, and power. As for Grievous's mental state, however, the augmentations did little to settle his mind and led to increased anger, lashing out at all those he perceived as weak, often destroying the droids placed under his care and leadership, for in some ways they reminded him of his own weaknesses. One [[Standard day|day]], Grievous was fatally injured in a [[Sabotage of Grievous' shuttle|sabotaged]] [[Grievous' shuttle|shuttle]] crash during [[San Hill]]'s attempted [[assassin]]ation,{{Topps|set=2019 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|cardname=General Grievous}} nearly killing him''[[Star Wars: A Galaxy at War]]'' and destroying most of what remained of his original body. When his [[troop carrier]] crashed, Grievous was flung from the wreckage{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} (German edition) and was taken from his homeworld and given a rare opportunity to become a living weapon. Rumors would later be spread that the crash was orchestrated by Dooku, which was indeed the case. Following the horrific shuttle crash that nearly took his life, the Kaleesh warlord regained consciousness in a [[bacta tank]] and discovered that [[FX-series medical assistant droid|surgical FX droids]] had nearly totally gutted and deformed him.{{BuildXWingCite|47|Starfighter Aces}} (German edition) Dooku claimed that the sabotage was carried out by a Jedi, since then fueling Grievous's deep and violent hatred for them. Betrayed and abused, with his sanity broken and mind fractured, Grievous accepted the offer of life-saving surgery and reconstruction and to return to military service, motivated by his hatred for the Republic and the Yam'rii. [[File:BountyHunters16-50yearstextless.png|thumb|right|300px|General Grievous, the cybernetic apprentice and servant of Count Dooku]] Even though Dooku was directly responsible for the shuttle crash that resulted in Grievous's injuries and subsequent transformation, Grievous was obviously psychologically confused with his final appearance. No evidence, at the end of the day, existed that Grievous was a victim in someone's grand design: despite Dooku's actions, Grievous had already decided to become a cyborg and was in that process no matter the Count's actions. Later historical work even disregarded the idea that Dooku was involved in the general's reconstruction as a shadowy manipulator due to evidence from Grievous's own life: it had been Grievous himself who wanted to be changed into a cyborg, no matter what role Dooku played in the final steps. Separatist [[Cyberneticist|cybernetic experts]] and [[Geonosian]] [[biotechnician]]s surgically reconstructed Grievous with assistance from [[medical droid]]s, including the [[FX-9 surgical assistant]] [[FX-6]], under the supervision of Count Dooku and Darth Sidious. Along with repairs and improvements provided by the Geonosian biotechs, some areas of Grievous' [[brain]] were altered without his knowledge, such as the installation of [[heuristic combat programming]], to make him a smarter, faster fighter.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' Furthermore, his demeanor was made more aggressive, memory centers were tinkered with to suppress recollections of his past and concentrate more, and areas of his brain dealing with coordination were modified to make it easier to utilize his cyborg body. Circuitry was grafted onto brain tissue, and wiring transports the brain's electrical impulses throughout the body. Although [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] implants were fitted to improve his vision and protect them from the [[vacuum]] of [[Realspace|space]], Grievous preserved his native [[Reptile|reptilian]] [[eye]]s, with enough skull remaining to prevent the organic muscles and tendons required for them to function as normally. His [[lung]]s were given implants as well. Many critical decisions were made regarding what should be kept of his original body. By the time the Kaleesh warrior had been rebuilt, very little remained of his original body, largely consisting only of portions of his brain, much of his spinal cord, spinal column, and parts of his head, including his eyes, and a few other vital organs, including his cold [[heart]], a pair of damaged lungs, a [[liver]], and the portions of his digestive system needed to maintain his organic elements. His brain and eyes were transplanted into a [[duranium]] alloy body, many of which were sculpted to resemble bone instead of [[metal]], while his remaining vital organs were protected in a pressurized [[synthskin]] gut-sack behind armored [[rib]]s, allowing him to operate in space without the need for a [[Environment suit|spacesuit]]. His form was completed with an [[LX-44 robotic leg]], powerfully magnetized, four talon-like feet, and [[Electrodriver|electro-driven]] mechanical [[Limb|arms]] that could be split at the dislocating shoulders and become four, turning him into a four-armed cyborg monstrosity. Each hand, with its own opposable thumb and articulated finger, integrated [[sensor]]s for feeling and touching the world.[[Age of Republic - General Grievous 1|''Age of Republic - General Grievous'' 1]] More machine than flesh. All that was left were metal, mechanical [[actuator]]s, armorplast, and hatred. [[File:GrievousBrain-RotSVD.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A cut-away of Grievous's head.]] Grievous's [[armor]], made of [[durasteel]] composite duranium and [[armorplast]], was significantly easier to make and maintain than [[Mandalorian]] [[beskar]], while not being as impenetrable. A head unit held parts of his skull and some of his brain, equipped two [[antenna]]es[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] and an [[Audio sensor|audio receptor]], and could be opened for repairs or replacement of electronics or for further surgery. Although Grievous’s spinal cord carried signals to and from his robotic limbs and body, as well as the organ contents of his gutsack, millions of pin-point [[electrode]]s were inserted into his brain from the lining of his [[helmet]] to [[Computer monitor|monitor]] brain activity and increase nerve signal timeliness. Adding to his already remarkable physical control, more processors improved agility and response times. Grievous's designers utilized [[crystal]] circuitry to improve reaction times as much as the technology allowed while remaining safe behind duranium plate armor. The technology that was used for Grievous's conversion into a cyborg wasn't perfect; his heart and lungs were weakened, with those lungs irritated by their implants, giving him a persistent cough for the rest of his life and, eventually, difficulty breathing. That information was in the Sith's possession in case they had additional candidates for conversion in the future. Due to his already compromised lungs, his speech occasionally degraded into a rasping, random coughing fit. He does not require to breathe, eat, or drink and can survive in a vacuum as well as underwater, immune to [[poison]]s and toxins. [[File:Kaleesh_statues2.png|thumb|right|270px|Statues of Grievous's transformation.]] While he claimed his old form was no more than weak flesh, Grievous retained several reminders of his past life. As a cyborg, Grievous frequently wore a [[Kaleesh cloak]], which was a vestige of his past identity, as well as a fearsome mask that was often worn by Kaleesh warriors. By the time he owned his [[Grievous's fortress|fortress]] on [[Vassek 3]], Grievous had several [[Statues of Grievous|statues]] lining the halls of the privacy of his inner sanctuary that depicted his progression from his organic life into that of a cyborg.{{SW|url=video/behind-the-scenes-lair-of-grievous|text=Behind the Scenes: Lair of Grievous}} As evidenced by the statues, some accounts claimed he was already a cyborg when Count Dooku recruited him to lead the droid army. Ironically, Grievous despised his completely mechanical [[militia]], possibly revealing at deeper thoughts about his own drastic change. Driven by ''[[Star Wars: Book of Lists]]'' his desire to become the greatest''[[Knights of Fate]]'' and superior warrior in the galaxy, the old, greatly feared Kaleesh warrior''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' claimed that he had his entire body altered{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Jedi Temple Archives|cardname=General Grievous|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022641/2015-Topps-Star-Wars-Chrome-Perspectives:-Jedi-Vs.-Sith-37-J-General-Grievous}} to increase his strength and extend his life in an attempt to give himself an advantage and compete with a Jedi in battle.{{HelmetCollectionCite|30|Databank A-Z}} Regardless of how he came to be, whether this was true or not, the former Kaleesh warlord went through numerous more operations to become soon-to-be General Grievous, the towering monster that stalked the galaxy. The cyborg's body was purposefully designed to resemble Grievous's Kaleesh body and warlord armor.{{BuildR2Cite|53|Droid Directory}} Among these were arms constructed to mimic the limbs he had been born with and a faceplate that mirrored the mask he formerly wore, paying homage to his former life and evoking his people's culture.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Collector's Edition|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' – The Official Collector's Edition]] As seen on his mask and chest-plate, these engraved lines resembled the patterns of war paint. In addition, the mask resembled his snub nose in overall outline, and the duranium teeth resembled the karabbac beast's teeth, as well as the bony protrusions on his chin. An [[ultrasonic vocabulator]] located behind the duranium teeth, where his [[mouth]] would have been if he had one at all, created and amplified Grievous's harsh, powerful voice and almost perfectly matched his original voice. Though the cyborg's [[Skeleton|skeletal]] structure bore various callbacks to his Kaleesh heritage, the vast majority of resemblance to other Kaleesh was eliminated; he still bore the distinctive [[snake]]-like beady [[Color|golden]] eyes with slit pupils and eyelids, flat [[nose]], and elongated [[ear]]s of his species, and the surrounding dark, tortured skin extended upward somewhat beneath the forehead of his faceplate. At first inspection, a small amount of residual red flesh around his eyes indicated the reptilian ancestry of the Kaleesh speckles, which was the only thing that belied his being's cyborg nature, horribly alive behind his inanimate steel mask. As stated, only his eyes remained the same as he had once been, and looking into them was like gazing into the gaping maw of a [[black hole]]. =====Trained by Count Dooku===== [[File:CountDookuDeviousStrategist-SWDA.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous was taught the Jedi martial arts by the Jedi-turned-Sith Lord Count Dooku, well-known for his swordsmanship.]] Grievous was initially handed a [[lightsaber|weapon]]—the [[Grievous' first lightsaber|one that belonged]] to an [[Unidentified Jedi (friend of Dooku)|old friend long dead]] of the former Jedi—by Dooku and, afterward, continued to add other weapons to the collection he had started when he was still a warlord on Kalee. Furious that his body had been entirely replaced with that of the droids he hated despite it being his own wish to become a cyborg that put him down such a path, Grievous immediately slaughtered all the guards present at his resurrection. Disgusted by his cyborg body, Grievous reluctantly accepted the job of Supreme Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies. He spent [[Standard hour|hours]] on end watching [[holovid]]s of Jedi in combat and reading all the training manuals the Count could supply him with. When it came to dealing with death, Grievous was a voracious learner, and to him, the differing saber styles were essentially extra military techniques to learn. He was then selected out for [[Lightsaber combat|lightsaber training]] by none other than Count Dooku, the [[Jedi]]-turned-[[Sith Lord|Sith-Lord]], who was regarded as a legendary swordsman. A combination of Dooku's instruction and a combat program, he has mastered several of the classic forms of Jedi arts and derived his impressive, extremely effective fighting style. While Dooku trained Grievous in Jedi martial arts, he retrained{{EncyclopediaCite|Darth Maul and Other Followers of the Dark Side}} and passed all of his knowledge to his IG-100 MagnaGuards to assure their success in fighting and later would employ them as sparring partners to keep himself sharp. Grievous received a modified [[EV-series medical droid]] [[EV-A4-D]] as a gift to serve as his [[Doctor|surgeon]] and cybernetics repair [[Technician|mechanic]]. With access to all of Grievous's medical and cybernetic records and a substantially increased intelligence, the fairly caustic and sometimes sadistic droid became the perfect foil for Grievous and his doctor. A4-D continued indispensability, giving him an inflated sense of self-worth and one of the few beings in the galaxy who understand his master's secrets. Although his caustic humor irritated Grievous, A4-D was allowed to survive as long as he completed his duty. Grievous owned a massive [[roggwart]] named [[Gor]], whom he kept in his [[fortress]] as a pet and guard [[dog]],{{BuildFalconCite|65|Guide to the Galaxy}} and expressed true care for him. Grievous altered and improved his cybernetic body, with A4-D helping to create and install the new components he asked for. In this regard, his claim that he chose his own modifications could be considered true from a particular twisted perspective in addition to the literal perspective. Grievous also had EV-A4-D enhanced Gor by attaching four cybernetic limbs to his back, an [[Exoskeleton/Canon|exoskeleton]] of battle armor to his body, and, like himself, a chest plate and helmet to protect his vital organs and braincase. ===The Clone Wars=== ====Early efforts==== =====General of the Confederacy===== {{Quote|The droid general, Grievous, has our forces spread thin.|Mace Windu|[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]}} Beyond receiving cybernetic enhancements, Grievous was trained in lightsaber combat by Dooku, who invited him to join his [[Separatist Crisis|Separatist movement]]. Grievous accepted the invitation{{HelmetCollectionCite|21|Databank A-Z}} and allied himself with other members of the Confederacy and its leading [[Executive Separatist Council]]. One member of the group was San Hill, the same Muun who was, unbeknownst to Grievous, secretly behind the assassination attempt. All of them entrusted to him and Dooku their invaluable resources and large droid armies.{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|42|Starships and Vehicles}} Grievous was in direct opposition of the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order, whom he had long regarded as mortal enemies. According to legend, although Grievous had the outward appearance of a machine, Grievous was pleased, for he alone understood his true potential and that he still had some of what made him a living, breathing man. He believed that set him apart from the rest of the Separatists, droids and organics alike. However, neither droids nor organics found themselves comfortable in his company. [[File:GalaxyofHeroes-Droid-Army.png|right|thumb|300px|General Grievous was at the head of vast and powerful armies of battle droids.]] The CIS and Republic were soon launched into opposite warring sides of the [[The galaxy|galactic]] conflict known as the Clone Wars with the [[First Battle of Geonosis|Battle of Geonosis]], which Grievous secretly took part in, though he was not seen. While it was entirely by accident, Grievous's first clash against members of the Jedi Order came during the battle. He was positioned within the [[Stalgasin hive]] [[Geonosian catacombs|catacombs]] on [[Geonosis]] when the battle began, and while retreating, the cyborg ended up dueling a number of Jedi who incidentally wandered into the tunnels in the midst of the battle. Grievous prevented the Jedi and the [[clone trooper]]s from reaching the Separatist Council and escaped through the hive tunnels beneath Geonosis, leaving none of the [[Force-sensitive]]s he encountered alive to speak of his existence.''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' As such, his involvement in the war's opening battle was not discovered by the Republic until much later. Grievous was quickly granted the rank of [[General]] in the [[Confederacy military]] and took upon the title of [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies]], with which he acted as [[Commander-in-Chief]] and absolute leader of the [[Separatist Droid Army]].''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' Furthermore, he was the most fearsome warrior of the Separatists.{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars Holocron Series|cardname=General Grievous}} In the early weeks of the war, he publicly emerged onto the scene as a major Separatist leader.[[Brotherhood (novel)|''Brotherhood'']] As later proclaimed in the legend he made for himself, Grievous swiftly became accomplished during his tenure, and he had risen in the ranks as a result of the many campaigns he had fought on behalf of his masters, claiming victory after victory. He earned a name for himself amongst the powerful figures leading the Separatist movement, in part because of his sheer commitment to being the best soldier he could be. The legend stated that it was soon after that that Grievous found himself promoted to the rank of general and given command of vast armies and fleets. [[File:Displate-GrievousDarkSide.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous expanded his lightsaber collection over the course of the Clone Wars by killing and defeating various Jedi.]] During the early weeks of the war, Grievous had an encounter with Jedi Master [[Ki-Adi-Mundi]], whom he wounded,''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' leaving the [[Cerean]] with scars across his cheek that took time to heal. Grievous was a dangerous''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Clone Troopers]]'' and key Separatist leader[[Star Wars Day-at-a-Time Calendar 2021|''Star Wars'' Day-at-a-Time Calendar 2021]] in the Separatist' hopes to overthrow the Republic.{{Shatterpoint|set=Appetite for Destruction Squad Pack}} Grievous brought a new wave of fear, and with it the threat of panic and chaos across the [[galaxy]]; the war expanded faster than the Republic could comprehend, and there was now a very real chance of losing.[[Obi-Wan 3|''Obi-Wan'' 3]] Grievous outperformed every [[Republic officer|command officer]] in the Republic,{{ForceCollection|General Grievous [Elusive Commander]|star=5}} using brutal tactics to lead the Confederacy{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|subset=Scum & Villainy|cardname=General Grievous}} to claim numerous victories in a series of battles, instilling fear in his opponents, and became the best and most important Separatist general and top military mind. He became Count Dooku's most powerful enforcer and his most foremost battlefield commander. The news of his abilities, and subsequent victories, caused doubt in the Republic's military ranks, as well as pure fear in the hearts of his victims. With his combat prowess in battle and his own fleet of specialized killing machines and vehicles, he immediately gained a reputation as a savage, merciless brute, military leader, and tactical genius. His name became notorious and terrified residents of Republic worlds, and, due to his choice of battle tactics, associated with the most extreme forms of violence and slaughter, Grievous became a legendary figure. As the Clone War proceeded to spread throughout the galaxy, Grievous and his forces engaged the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], and, under his command, the Separatist Droid Army attacked and conquered numerous Republic planets.{{Databank|confederacy-of-independent-systems|Confederacy of Independent Systems}} Overall, Grievous won many victories for the Confederacy{{Topps|set=2025 Topps Star Wars Chrome|subset=Double Vision|cardname=DV-12 General Grievous|link=https://www.ebay.com/itm/306602524721|archivedate=20251230013627}} and brought significant devastation to the innocent inhabitants of the galaxy. With four arms, four lightsabers, and a complete army behind him''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]'' that he could lead to victory, he sliced through vast sections of the Republic forces. Considered invincible, Grievous was the most feared individual, certainly by those on the Republic side and many in the Separatist forces, in the galaxy. As the Separatist Army's imposing leader, Grievous and the tales of his brutality and victories would strike fear throughout the Republic,{{Databank|general-grievous|General Grievous}} although the Confederate populace were not told the stories of the general's bloody onslaughts.{{SWE|characters|minabonteri|Mina Bonteri}} Ultimately, many Republic citizens—as well as some citizens in CIS territory—came to see Grievous as the face of the Confederacy despite Dooku's status as its official leader. Those who knew the Kaleesh warrior's true nature saw this face as a brutal and terrifying one.{{Databank|url=confederacy-of-independent-systems-history-gallery|title=Confederacy of Independent Systems History Gallery}} {{C|Image 9 caption}} Anyone observing Grievous march forth would understandably find it difficult to accept he wasn't completely a machine.{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/databank-download-general-grievous|text=Databank Download: General Grievous|date=2023-05-30}} Grievous also share his name with [[The Grievous Legion]], a [[battle group]] that included at least one [[Vulture-class starfighter|vulture droid]].[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] [[File:Clone-War-battlefront.png|thumb|right|270px|Grievous leads one of his armies against the Republic.]] During the war, the clone troopers of the [[Republic Military]],{{TCW|Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence''}} having nicknamed the Confederacy's battle droids "clankers,"{{TCW|Ambush}} accordingly nicknamed Grievous the "head clanker;" Grievous was also referred to within the Republic as the "droid general." While the war against the Yam'rii had given Grievous a vendetta against the Republic, the Clone Wars had changed him; indifferent to the Republic and the politics of the war as a whole, his only goal was to see the extermination of the Jedi Order, which led to him escalating the war as his quest to wipe out the Jedi once and for all carried on. Only Grievous's hatred of Jedi and his unwavering faith in his own abilities gave those standing against him a chance. Grievous took part in numerous battles and skirmishes and fought against numerous Jedi during the war, defeating and killing many of the Order's members, which allowed the general to quickly acquire a large number and horrific collection of lightsabers and other prizes as a preeminent{{InsiderCite|230|A Certain Point of View}} and feared [[Jedi hunter]]. Using his lifetime of knowledge and the benefits of his mechanical body directed by the distorted mentality of a physically damaged warrior, Grievous was deadly and proved himself to be a powerful opponent, more than equal to his Jedi foes, especially if they did not act carelessly. He was one of the galaxy's greatest fighters and perhaps individually responsible for more Jedi deaths during the war than anybody else. Little was known about his possible use of the Force, suggesting that he could be more difficult to find than others. Grievous often maintained a strategy of elusiveness, making it difficult for the Republic's forces to locate him despite it being one of their primary objectives. Defiant by temperament, he never hesitated to challenge his opponents and frequently masterminded intricate, audacious plans that left the Republic's troops embarrassed. =====Duels with Kenobi===== {{Quote|I was told the Jedi was restrained.''"
"''Terribly sorry to disappoint you. I'm going to need you to release Senator Yarua and his daughter.''"
"''It's ''my'' turn to disappoint ''you.|Grievous duels Obi-Wan Kenobi|[[Hyperspace Stories 1|''Hyperspace Stories'' 1]]}} During the war, Grievous came to duel Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] numerous times, developing a history between them that made it so Grievous would choose to engage Kenobi over others. Grievous harbored a deep hatred for Kenobi.{{Topps|set=2019 Topps Star Wars Chrome Legacy|cardname=Specializing in Sith Lords}} Their confrontation turned the two into mortal adversaries, and their immense abilities were evenly matched.{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Sith Fugitives|cardname=General Grievous|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/117731/cid/8023186/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith---Sith-Fugitives-4-General-Grievous}} Each time was inconclusive, but both realized that this could not always be the case. Kenobi's apprentice, [[Jedi]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], considered him a monster that needed to be stopped, even making it a personal mission to find Grievous. However, Grievous and Skywalker would not meet face-to-face until the war had nearly reached its conclusion. As Kenobi, his [[Padawan]] apprentice Anakin Skywalker, and Senator Amidala were on a [[Unidentified secret mission|secret mission]] to meet with the [[Rodian]] [[The Ambassador|ambassador]] on a [[Unidentified planet (Clone Wars)|planet]], Grievous had dispatched several [[B1-series battle droid]]s and a [[Unidentified MSE droid (Grievous)|modified]] [[MSE series|MSE droid]] to infiltrate their [[Consular-class light cruiser|''Consular-class space cruiser'']]. Then, Grievous appeared on their screen to reveal that everything was proceeding as planned, Kenobi was correct to assume he was involved, and Grievous understands his concerns. Grievous ordered his droids to attack, he knew that the facilities were defeatable. He now reveals his true intention, knowing that there was nothing they can do to stop him. Grievous successfully reprogrammed their ship's [[flight computer]], irreversibly directing them into the [[star|sun]].[[Star Wars: My First Comic Reader 1|''Star Wars: My First Comic Reader'' 1]] Grievous explained to Padmé that while they were luckily against fighting battle droids, a little droid snuck into their ship. While Anakin instructed Obi-Wan to remain in command, Padme assured him that they would handle the droid, but Grievous reminded them that they cannot stop his droid in the same way they cannot change the direction of the ship and then ordered the droid to eliminate the Senator and the two Jedi. However, Kenobi and Skywalker took back control of the ship by having the mouse droid shoot at the control panel, and then the two Jedi destroyed the mouse droid, leaving only Grievous to admit defeat. Towards the beginning of the war, Grievous led a fleet of [[Providence-class Dreadnought|''Providence''-class Dreadnoughts]] to the [[Moon of Staggec]] with the aim of taking a [[Unidentified Jedi artifact|valuable item]] from Republic Senator [[Yarua]]. There, he and his droid forces [[Mission to the moon of Staggec|captured]] Yarua, [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], and their associates. Shortly after, the droids also captured Yarua's daughter [[Viiveenn]] and Kenobi. Once Kenobi was restrained, Grievous interrogated Yarua and Viiveenn about their hidden item. Just then, Kenobi appeared behind Grievous and asked for Yarua and Viiveenn to be released. Grievous responded by drawing his lightsabers and engaging the Jedi in combat. [[Force push]]ed by Kenobi, Grievous immediately took Viiveenn hostage, only for Yarua to tackle him into space, sacrificing himself and allowing his daughter to escape along with the Jedi. While successfully escaping from the Separatists, Kenobi assumed Grievous was dead, but Yoda warned him not to underestimate him. =====Victories and defeats===== [[File:ADAndGrievous-JOTRMaceWindu3.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous and AD-W4.]] Shortly into the war, Grievous met in person with the droid [[mercenary]] [[AD-W4]] to hire him to oversee the Separatists' operations on the planet [[Hissrich]]. Grievous admitted that he would have liked to fill this role himself, but could not as he had the entire Separatist Droid Army to command. AD-W4 was skeptical, but after seeing the [[Currency|payment]] available, left to fulfill the job. AD-W4 served as [[commander]] of the droids on the planet and [[Operation on Hissrich|battled]] with Jedi Master [[Mace Windu]] and his [[Mace Windu's squad|Jedi squad]]. Grievous later checked in via [[hologram]] to see the progress of AD-W4, and the droid falsely claimed to have killed Windu; however Grievous demanded the [[Mace Windu's lightsaber|Jedi's lightsaber]] as evidence, which was not presented.[[Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu 3|''Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu'' 3]] Ultimately, the droid was defeated and Hissrich was lost to the Republic.[[Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu 5|''Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu'' 5]] A while later, around the time of an [[Mission to Cato Neimoidia (Kenobi and Skywalker)|incident]] on [[Cato Neimoidia]], Grievous [[Strike on key supply chains for war munitions|struck on key supply chains for war munitions]]. Early in the war, Grievous launched an assault that failed to [[Attempt to capture Outpost 716|capture]] [[Outpost 716]], forcing Count Dooku to dispatch his personal [[Sith assassin|assassin]] and [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], [[Asajj Ventress]], in [[Capture of Outpost 716|another attempt to capture]] the outpost. Darth Sidious doubts Dooku's faith in his two students, however, Ventress successfully captured Outpost 716. Soon after [[Ambush on the moon of Staggec|surviving an ambushed]], Ventress informs Dooku that it appears someone slipped information to Chancellor Palpatine that she would be returning to clean up Grievous's mess.[[Hyperspace Stories 5|''Hyperspace Stories'' 5]] In the [[Battle of Parein II 4|battle]] on the [[Parein II 4|fourth moon]] of [[Parein II]] saw the first real test of the IG-100 MagnaGuards, and on the battlefield, Grievous used a new weapon for the first time: the [[TSMEU-6 personal wheel bike]].{{EncyclopediaCite|Miscellaneous Ships and Vehicles (2)}} With Grievous in command and leading his troops at the front, the Republic forces led by Jedi General [[Sannen]]{{EncyclopediaCite|Battle Droids and Other Droids of War}} (English version) were utterly crushed. Sannen bravely tried to confront the cyborg directly, but the Jedi was instead stabbed in the [[throat]] with an [[electrostaff]]-wielding MagnaGuard. The IG-100 MagnaGuards quickly became as feared as their master, were synonymous with Grievous, and shared his fearsome reputation, rarely seen without at least two by his side, forming a shield around him few could pass. According to legend, early in the Clone Wars, Grievous was tasked with a critical mission; he was to travel to the distant [[Water|ice]] planet [[Alamass]] and deploy his army of droids in an [[Battle of Alamass|assault]] that would destroy a strategic enemy [[Republic stronghold|stronghold]]. The operation was a dangerous and difficult one, at which Grievous ultimately failed due to his [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Alamass)|tactical droid's]] betrayal. Grievous decided to take the risk even though sending an army there would have cost him a third of his droids along the way, and as he prepared to deploy an army of droids to the planet, his tactical droid disobeyed his programming by altering the plan Grievous had given the Droid Army: Grievous's orders would lead to Separatist victory. Eventually, the general was forced to admit his defeat to his Sith masters, becoming Grievous's first major loss. At some point, Grievous and Jedi Knight [[Pablo-Jill]] had a [[Duel over Duro|duel]] over the world of [[Duro]] in a [[Unidentified satellite city|collapsing satellite city]]. Jill was left injured and lost his blue-[[Plasma|bladed]] [[Pablo-Jill's lightsaber|lightsaber]] to Grievous.''[[Star Wars Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]'' At some point, Grievous killed Jedi Master [[Jmmaar]] and took his green-bladed [[Jmmaar's lightsaber|lightsaber]] in order to add to his own collection.[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] =====Venture to the Haven===== {{Quote|This negotiation is over.''"

You will be destroyed, but at least I can make use of your ''parts''.|Telemak and Grievous|[[Bounty Hunters 38|''Bounty Hunters'' 38]]}} [[File:GrievousDestroysDroids-BountyHunters38.png|thumb|right|235px|Grievous destroyed numerous droids on The Haven.]] With the coordinates from [[Tarr Kligson]], a member of the [[Kligson clan]] who operated as a [[bounty hunter]],[[Bounty Hunters 37|''Bounty Hunters'' 37]] Grievous [[Skirmish on The Haven|traveled]] with two IG-100 MagnaGuards and several B1 battle droids to a large [[space station]], [[Haven (droid outpost)|the Haven]], orbiting [[Kligson's Moon]] in a [[Kligson's Moon's sector|sector]].[[Revelations (2022) 1|''Revelations'' (2022) 1]] Grievous arrived to offer [[Telemak]], the station's protector, the protection of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, but Telemak, knowing what Grievous wanted—more droids to join the Separatist Droid Army—interrupted him before he could finish and insulted him, suggesting that he couldn't beat the Galactic Republic with those he currently "enslaves." Grievous was dissatisfied that they would stay here and deteriorate, waiting for their leader, [[Ajax Sigma]], to come back rather than seizing the chance he provided them to [[Battle on Kligson's Moon|inflict revenge on the Jedi Order that had destroyed him]]. Before his next statement, Telemak declared that they do not serve organics, concluded the discussions, and surrounded him with droids. Grievous happily accepts and, tired of diplomacy, attacks Telemak and its droid army. And you will do as I say… Or you will ''die''.|Grievous after capturing Kenobi|[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 5|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 5]]}} [[File:GrievousAndKenobiInTheSnow-TCWBattleTales5.jpg|thumb|left|290px|Grievous and Kenobi duel on the frozen moon of Caliban.]] Grievous [[Battle on Caliban|attacked]] the frozen moon of [[Caliban]] after he [[Invasion of Caliban|invaded]] the moon and destroyed a [[Lunar ice bridge|lunar bridge]] in the procession. He also [[Prisoner|captured]] Jedi General Kenobi and [[Clone Marshal Commander]] [[Cody]], along with their [[squad]] of clone troopers and ordered them to rebuild the bridge, to allow him to freely move weapons and battle droids across the moon. Kenobi, however, answered that he and the clones would not have to work for Grievous, since according to the [[Galactic Accord of Systems]], no war prisoner could be forced into manual labor. The Separatist general smacked Kenobi to the ground and threatened him with death if he would not follow his orders. Kenobi and the clones started constructing the bridge, but, during the operation, Grievous was distracted by a group of native [[Qubey]]s, in league with Kenobi, who piled on top of him and managed to steal back [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber|Kenobi's lightsaber]], which had been tucked into Grievous's cloak, without the cyborg noticing. Although the bridge was completed sometime later, Grievous ordered the battle droids to execute Kenobi and his men, but the Qubeys ambushed the droids, allowing Kenobi to engage Grievous while the clones reclaimed their [[blaster]]s. In the ensuing battle, Grievous overwhelmed Kenobi, but when he was right where the Master wanted him, Kenobi used the Force to cause an avalanche, burying Grievous and his droids. Kenobi and the clones escaped on a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry]] [[gunship]], realizing that staying to capture Grievous would put the Qubey further in danger, and they destroyed the bridge before Separatist reinforcements could arrive. ====Attack on the ''Stellar Rise''==== {{Quote|Tell me about the hilt you have found. I have been monitoring your mission here in the Outer Rim to collect rare Jedi artifacts from the High Republic Era.|Grievous, to Anap Ree-Di|{{InsiderCite|210|Galactic Tales: Saber Truth}}}} At some point during the Clone Wars, Grievous [[Infiltration of the Stellar Rise|infiltrated]] the [[Arquitens-class light cruiser|''Arquitens''-class light cruiser]] ''[[Stellar Rise]]'' and brought along four IG-100 MagnaGuards aboard with the intent of stealing [[High Republic Era|High Republic–era]] [[Jedi artifact|artifacts]]. While taking inventory of crates that had been picked up near the [[Kazlin system]], [[Checkbox]] noticed something off about the boxes he was going through from the one closest to him that sounded like a [[stone mite]]-like. A blue lightsaber from Grievous sliced through Checkbox, hacking him in two vertically. Upon entering the bridge, the MagnaGuards quickly dispatched the entire deck crew in under a [[Standard minute|minute]]. Grievous spared the ship's [[Captain]] [[Lozz Beraf]], intimidating him, but then Jedi Knight [[Anap Ree-Di]] showed up and ordered him to let go of the captain and leave. His attention was caught by her piercing green eyes with a crystal-gaze and her apparent confidence, but he had yet to demonstrate his potential to her. Grievous slowly produced four lightsabers, activated them one by one, and displayed a menacing demeanor. She remained motionless; her gaze locked on him. As the Jedi was about to be struck by all four MagnaGuards jumping forward, swinging their electrostaffs, she managed to draw [[Anap Ree-Di's lightsaber|her green lightsaber]], blocking their attacks and somersaulting backwards to dodge the others, landing like a [[loth-cat]]. [[File:SaberTruthCover.png|thumb|right|264px|Grievous was on the search for Jedi artifacts from the High Republic Era.]] Grievous stopped his droids' assault, and she quickly fled the bridge. He commanded his troops to follow her, removing his [[cape]] off the deck, and moved forward. They tracked the fleeing Jedi to a small area of the ship identified as the [[barracks]], and Grievous stopped his troops' approach outside the main door. All around them, a wailing alarm went off; Captain Lozz must've activated it. While disregarding the roaring sounds, Grievous told his guards the three-word key elements. The Jedi mocked Grievous, once more emerging out of nowhere, attacking unexpectedly from behind, and severed one of the MagnaGuards' arms while it wielded an electrostaff. The remaining three droids launched their attack, delivering blow after blow on the Jedi's green blade repeatedly and driving her out of the barracks. Now, Grievous ignited two lightsabers and closed in for the kill. At that point, four clone troopers emerged, armed with weapons of their own. As they, too, struck from the rear, the MagnaGuards were caught off guard, and one of them was almost totally dissolved. Snarled in anger, Grievous flung one of his lightsabers in a low arc, slicing through the two clones' legs. After retrieving his weapon, he shifted his focus to the problematic Jedi, drawing three more from his cloak and charging toward her at speed. To his utter joy, he noticed a fleeting glimmer of confusion rather than terror, but regardless of her emotions, Grievous saw the Jedi retreating and would soon have her cornered. His adversary used the Force with a movement of her hand to open a [[blast shield]] behind her and stepped through it backwards, almost losing her footing. Grievous brought down two of his blades on her, which she parried, while the other two swept low and almost took out her legs. The seemed prepared Anap simply soared above the lightsabers and kicked Grievous's chest as the movement of his two lower arms unbalanced him. He pressed his attack once more, nearly disarming the Jedi with a maneuver meant to catch her by surprise. For a minute, Grievous took a step back, and the Jedi did something unusual. Her hand waved once more and the shield lowered, separating them from the battle between the IG-100 droids and the troopers. Again, Grievous found it very amusing that she might have believed he was defenseless without the MagnaGuards. He instructed her to inform him of the [[Lightsaber hilt|hilt]] she had discovered and that he had been keeping an eye on her mission in search of rare Jedi artifacts in the Outer Rim. Aware that she was bringing them all securely back to the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]], where the [[Archivist]] examines and files them in some dusty room. Anap informed Grievous that Master [[Jocasta Nu]] had described her as having an "[[Soul|old soul]]," to which he replied that would soon be all that remained of her. Grievous moved forward, spinning his lightsabers at near-impossible speeds, intent on striking a fatal blow. In a pitiful attempt at defense, she threw her ignited lightsaber at him, and he watched as it went harmlessly by, landing in an ancillary walkway. Ultimately, Grievous was tricked into entering an escape pod by Ree-Di, and the Republic ship jumped to [[lightspeed]], leaving him alone and adrift in space. ====The ''Malevolence'' campaign==== {{Quote|General Kenobi. Did you really think I would leave the hyperdrive unguarded?''"
