Dooku then ordered him to direct his entire droid fleet at Maul's recently formed crime syndicate—the [[Shadow Collective]] and ordered him to destroy his army and wound his pride, but not to kill him. This was in order for him to draw out Mother Talzin, Maul's mother and one of the most powerful beings in the galaxy. Grievous thought it foolish to keep Maul alive, but Dooku reminded Grievous that it was not wise to question the plans of Darth Sidious, and that he as Dooku's apprentice would carry out his orders to the fullest degree. Grievous then moved his fleet to Zanbar and launched several landing craft to destroy the [[Mandalorian warrior]]s, starting off the [[Battle of Zanbar]]. [[File:DarthMaulGrievousDuel.png|thumb|right|230px|Maul and Grievous engage in battle.]] Basing his calculation on their experience compared to the clones they normally fought, Grievous knew that the chances of his droid army gaining a victory in this battle were unlikely. Deploying his droids after telling them as such, Grievous watched the fighting unfold from a landing craft until he spotted Maul on the battlefield. After sending out four of his IG-100 MagnaGuards to weaken Maul, Grievous emerged from his ship and engaged at least one [[Mandalorian super commando]] in battle, easily killing him with his lightsabers. Maul disposed of the MagnaGuards and turned his attention to the cyborg general and engaged Grievous in single combat. Neither Maul nor Grievous was able to gain the upper hand in the duel, but Grievous, per his orders, taunted Maul, telling him that the battle was lost. However, Maul had held several [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport|Gauntlet fighters]] in reserve and ordered them to drop firebombs onto the battlefield. This left both factions' resources almost depleted. Maul, realizing Zanbar was lost, fled into a Gauntlet fighter and retreated from Grievous. Grievous then contacted Count Dooku via hologram and informed him he had fulfilled his master's wishes; Maul was on the run. Dooku then congratulated Grievous. Maul now believed the Sith were out to destroy him and his Syndicate, but would not learn of their true intentions until it was too late. Grievous knew their goal was the [[Dathomirian|witch]] Talzin, but did not understand what value Maul held for the Witch. Dooku told him all would be revealed as their plans unfolded. ====Captured by Maul==== {{Quote|Once our droids take control of the city, Maul's forces will be insects under our heels!|Grievous during the battle|[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 2|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 2]]}} [[File:CIS_Orbital_Bombardment_SoD.png|thumb|left|239x239px|Grievous orders for his ships to fire.]] After leaving Zanbar, Dooku rendezvoused with Grievous, gathering the fleet after Separatist spies reported that Mandalorian warships were amassing on the planet of [[Ord Mantell]], confirming Maul was in league with the [[Black Sun]] who controlled the planet. Grievous once again questioned the Dark Lord's obsession with destroying Mother Talzin; Dooku explained to Grievous that Talzin was an older and fouler creature than Grievous understood, and that she would have to be destroyed before she disrupted Darth Sidious' plans. Grievous' [[ST-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|super tactical droid]] [[Tey-Zuka]] reported to the cyborg general that a [[Talzin's shuttle|lone transport shuttle]] had left Dathomir moments ago, with Ord Mantell being a possible destination. Dooku believed Talzin was aboard and ordered the fleet to move to Ord Mantell. Soon they arrived and Grievous ordered the fleet to begin bombarding the [[Ord Mantell City|city]] from orbit. With the city now in ruins, the landing crafts began their assault. Grievous believed Maul's forces would soon be on the run but became suspicious when he realized he had not seen any Mandalorian warships. Tey-Zuka calculated that they had been destroyed before they could lift off but Grievous knew better—they were planning a sneak attack. The Gauntlet fighters appeared from behind Ord Mantell's moon, [[Battle on Ord Mantell|attacking]] the Separatist fleet. Grievous had been lured into a trap. Tey-Zuka reported a fighter had attached itself to the [[hull]] of Grievous' ''Providence''-class Dreadnought—but before the droid could finish, Maul interrupted. He gave Grievous an ultimatum; either he shut down the battle droids that were killing his troops—or he would die. With the general dismissing his threats, Maul then charged Grievous, tackling him into a [[transparisteel]] viewport. Dooku had also been captured as well. Maul contacted Sidious via hologram after traveling to [[Vizsla Keep 09]], threatening to kill them both unless he met Mother Talzin's demands. Sidious refused, instead stating he had no further use for them. Maul decided not to kill them, but ordered Grievous to the brig. Grievous told Dooku that it would be unfortunate if the next time they met he would have to add [[Dooku's lightsaber]] to his collection.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]] Dooku, who was still on the bridge of the ship, later used the Force to unlock Grievous' cell. Grievous escaped, killing the Mandalorians that were guarding him and several more while searching for a way off the ship. He soon found an escape pod, ejecting from the carrier and escaping from Maul. ====Confronting Talzin==== {{Quote|It is just as you predicted, my Lord...we've traced Count Dooku's signals to Dathomir's surface. What is your command?|Grievous to Darth Sidious just before the battle|[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 4|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 4]]}} Shortly afterward, Grievous regrouped with Darth Sidious aboard the ''[[Scimitar]]''; which was originally Maul's personal starship; and they made their way to Dathomir where Dooku's signals were emanating from; just as Sidious predicted. Sidious ordered Grievous to [[Cloaking device|cloak]] the ship from view and make their way to Dathomir's surface. They landed and the pair approached a chamber said to hold a stone column that was the heart of Mother Talzin's power. The chamber was located very near the [[Nightbrother village]] where Maul was born. Grievous blew an opening in the wall of the chamber, entered and stated he was about to kill Maul. Sidious followed, stating only the Dark Lord's plan shall rule the galaxy. Dooku appeared, though he was now [[Possession|possessed]] by Talzin, who at the time was still unable to take physical form. [[File:Grievous_Owns_Talzin.png|thumb|right|225px|Grievous executes Talzin.]] The four [[Second Battle of Dathomir|engaged]] in lightsaber combat; Grievous attacked Maul while Sidious freed his apprentice from Talzin with the use of [[Force lightning]]. Talzin returned in the flesh while Sidious told her she was going to die here. Maul took advantage of this distraction and used the Force to shove Grievous through the opening the explosion had created. Sidious attacked Talzin with a Force lightning barrage while Talzin defended Maul and herself with [[magick]] as her son implored her to fight on. Dooku recovered and strengthened his master's assault against the witch. Knowing that escaping was impossible, Talzin threw Maul into his ship over his desperate objections. Grievous reentered the chamber calmly striding towards the now beaten Talzin; Grievous then ignited his lightsabers and bypassed her defenses and plunged them through the witch's chest, killing her for the second and final time{{HelmetCollectionCite|52|Databank A-Z}} and ending her renewed quest for ultimate power. As the Droid Army attacked the nearby [[Unidentified Nightbrother village|Nightbrother village]], Darth Sidious took a moment to congratulate Dooku and Grievous; Maul's future had been erased while theirs was more certain than it had ever been. At some point following these events,{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-chronological-episodeorder|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Chronological Episode Order}} {{C|version archived on [[June 29]], [[2017]]; now replaced}} the Confederacy launched an [[Second battle of Christophsis|effort]] to retake the planet Christophsis as revenge for its previous defeat.{{Databank|christophsis-history-gallery|Christophsis History Gallery}} {{C|Image caption 13}} Because of how personal winning the planet was to Dooku, Ventress suspected that Grievous would be involved in the battle. Having allied with the Jedi and the rescued Quinlan Vos to try and kill Dooku again, she informed the Jedi Council of such, but their efforts ended in failure when Dooku escaped and Ventress, acting to save Vos from being struck by Force lightning, appeared{{SW|url=news/the-bad-batch-season-3-trailer|text=Watch the ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season 3 Trailer}} to be mortally wounded. Grievous rescued Dooku, but Vos had redeemed himself.{{SW|url=quinlan-vos-biography-gallery|text=Quinlan Vos Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image caption 14}} ===The final days=== ====Fighting Billaba==== {{Quote|You and your Jedi whelp ''die'' today, Billaba.''"
"''We shall see, ''Grievous'', we shall see.''"
"''I defeated you once before. My mistake was not confirming your death. It is not an error I intend to repeat.|General Grievous and Depa Billaba|}} [[File:Grievous-Kanan9.png|thumb|left|190px|Grievous realized he would need to deal with the Jedi himself.]] Six months after his victory over Billaba, [[Rackham Sear]] and General [[Kleeve]] discuss the plan to attack the Jedi Temple on Coruscant and destroy the central tower, having paid the [[Duros]] bounty hunter [[Cad Bane]],[[Kanan 8|''Kanan'' 8]] who had [[Raid on the Jedi Temple|infiltrated]] the temple three years before, for the necessary information. While Kleeve was opposed Sear's idea and saw it as a suicide mission, Grievous backed Rackham, remarking his patriotism, and if the tower falls, both the Republic and Separatists will realize that neither the Jedi Order nor the Republic are invincible, thus changing the direction of the war. He and Kleeve then sent in their top explosive expert, Captain Rackham Sear, to carry out a [[Bombing at the Jedi Temple|bombing]] on the Jedi Temple. After Captain Sear's mission failure, Grievous then went to [[Kardoa]] with Kleeve and Sear's brother, [[Colonel]] [[Coburn Sear]]. There, Grievous saw Billaba [[Skirmish on Kardoa|leading]] the [[Depa Billaba's second battalion|Republic forces]]. Grievous then demanded that she must die. However, Kleeve saw his obsession with killing Jedi as a distraction and warned against attacking before he left for [[Kaller]]. Grievous left as well for [[Mygeeto]]. However, he left Colonel Sear to deal with Billaba and her forces. Grievous then waited for Billaba and her forces to come to Mygeeto. There, he and Colonel Sear [[Third Battle of Mygeeto|confronted]] Billaba and her apprentice, [[Kanan Jarrus|Caleb Dume]]. The general was able to quickly overwhelm her forces with dozens of battle droids when he demolished the bridges of the [[Southern Mesas|Mesa]], until the [[Fang-class Protectorate fighter|Fang fighters]] of [[Skull Squadron]] under [[Skull Leader]] [[Fenn Rau]] destroyed the battle droids that were attacking. After killing the nearby [[Stance|clone trooper]], Sear confronted Dume, and Grievous was able to duel Billaba again, brandishing two lightsabers[[Kanan 10|''Kanan'' 10]] and striking her repeatedly, believing that he had already defeated her and wouldn't repeat the mistake of failing to verify her death. Billaba blocked Grievous's every strike, responded that she was no longer the same person as before and saw herself as capable of defeating him, and hit Grievous with a Force push. He reappeared from behind her with two more blades and attacked her with two of them held aloft while the other two swept low, attempting to strike her down. However, she parried and severed two of Grievous's lower hands [[Depa Billaba's lightsaber|with her lightsaber]]. Grievous then severely injured Billaba, slashing her from behind, and despite that, she continued fighting until Dume, Commander [[Styles]], and Captain [[Grey (clone trooper)|Grey]] arrived to aid her. Grey and Styles opened fire on the general, but he deflected their blaster shots, spinning two of his lightsabers, while Dume proceeded to Billaba. Grievous forced a retreat before Billaba and Dume could even attempt to surround him from behind as he continued to deflect the blaster fire from the clones. Sliding down from the structure with his lightsabers, he regretted allowing her to live, leaving Mygeeto with the Republic. After the cyborg had fled, Billaba had long since learned to live with remorse and did not order a pursuit of him. ====Hiding the Separatist Council==== {{Quote|He is here. We are being held hostage. They are watching us. ''[…]'' Tenth level. Thousands of battle droids.|Tion Medon, on Grievous' occupation|}} Much to the disappointment of the [[Utapaun]]s, who they had hoped the prior defeat of General Grievous and the loss of the kyber crystal would restore relative obscurity to their world,{{HelmetCollectionCite|25|Highlights of the Saga}} [[Separatist high command]] decided to seek refuge on Utapau{{EncyclopediaCite|Saw Gerrera and Other Characters of the Galaxy}} when Grievous chose the planet as a hiding place for the Executive Separatist Council.[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] With it decided, Darth Sidious commanded key Separatist leaders to gather there. Within months of the arms deal,{{HelmetCollectionCite|61|Databank A-Z}} in the final weeks of the Clone Wars, Grievous returned, this time with an invading force,{{BuildR2Cite|40|Droid Directory}} along with the ''Soulless One'', commanding thousands of battle droids and a detachment of MagnaGuards, and led the secret [[invasion of Utapau]],{{EncyclopediaCite|Republic and Separatist Ships (2)}} and during this invasion, the [[General Grievous' TSMEU-6 Wheel Bike|TSMEU-6 wheel bike]] was the general's preferred vehicle.{{Databank|general-grievous-tsmeu-6-wheel-bike|General Grievous' TSMEU-6 Wheel Bike}} Grievous and his forces invaded their peaceful world, forcing their leaders to cooperate. He was unwilling to face opposition from the planet's ruling [[Utapaun Committee]] and ordered his MagnaGuards to kill all of their members, much to [[Tion Medon]]'s horror. With the threat of immediate destruction over [[Pau'an]]s and [[Utai]], the [[Port Administrator]] had no choice but to comply with Grievous's demands, and a small Confederate base in Pau City was established by Grievous, where, under orders from Sidious, the Separatist Council was safely hidden. Before long, a massively modified [[core ship]] had taken over much of the city's [[level 10]], serving as the command headquarters for the Separatist droid forces.{{SWE|locations|utapau|Utapau}} ====Outer Rim Sieges==== =====CIS on the brink===== Ultimately, the Republic held all the momentum for the third year of the war. Despite Grievous's successes on Dathomir, Florrum, and elsewhere, the Separatists lost the majority of their droid factories and territory, pushing them to the Outer Rim. In the campaign known as the [[Outer Rim Sieges]], the Republic Military kept up the pressure.''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]'' Several key Separatist worlds were blockaded as droids and clones clashed throughout the Outer Rim,{{TCW|A Distant Echo}} with fronts also able to be opened in the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] and [[Colonies]].{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}} During the sieges, Grievous attempted to take control of the [[Anaxes shipyards|shipyards]] on the planet [[Anaxes]]{{EncyclopediaCite|Droid Tanks and Vehicles, and Other Mechanicals}} on the Coreward edge of the Outer Rim, where the Republic owned a number of important [[shipyard]]s. Grievous's desire led to a protracted,{{EncyclopediaCite|Droid Tanks and Vehicles, and Other Mechanicals}} (English version) [[Battle of Anaxes|costly battle]] carried out by the [[Harch]] [[Admiral]] [[Trench]], who dispatched [[Trench's army|droid forces]] and attacked the Republic shipyards.{{TCW|The Bad Batch (episode)}} However, the conflict ended in a total defeat for the CIS, with Trench himself killed, his forces wiped out, and the Anaxes shipyards secured by the Republic.{{TCW|Unfinished Business (episode)}} Additionally, Grievous played a decisive role in the outbreak of conflict between the [[Wookiee]]s and the CIS after his battle droids used excessive force to convince the Wookiees to join the Separatists. Although the Separatists had already undertaken several small campaigns on the planet, they ultimately made the decision to concentrate their efforts on [[Kachirho]], a coastal city in the [[Wawaatt Archipelago]] surrounded by freshwater lakes. Grievous and the Separatists were interested in [[Kashyyyk]] in general, and Kachirho in particular, for another reason; Kachirho was a key place because it was simple to defend while also being an excellent landing strip for droids and was home to the [[Claatuvac Guild]] Archives, which contained many unknown space roads. Initially, the Wookiees attempted to remain neutral in the conflict, but the importance of the planet compelled both sides to enter into a series of negotiations with the [[Kashyyyk royal families|royal families]] of Kashyyyk to try and persuade them to join their cause. After a long wait for a favorable decision, Grievous became impatient and directed a large-scale attack, hoping the threat would "persuade" the Wookiees to accept the conditions posed by Dooku and his allies.{{HelmetCollectionCite|27|Highlights of the Saga}} (Spanish version) The decision, however, turned out to be a dire mistake for the Confederacy, and the Wookiees responded angrily, declaring an all-out war on the forces threatening to attack them, leading to the [[Battle of Kashyyyk]]. The invasion and occupation began with a failed attack on the [[Kashyyyk oil refinery|oil refinery]] near Kachirho City in an attempt to cut off [[fuel]] supplies and reverse their declining fortunes in the war with help from the Claatuvac Guild's information. For the conflict, Confederacy allied with the Wookiees' Trandoshan enemies and deployed a secret force of battle droids along with warships. At some point, Grievous loaned one of the lightsabers from his personal collection to Separatist propaganda agents, who used it to make a fake hologram that was meant to stir up hatred against the Jedi.''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]'' Towards the end of the war, the [[Crispus Commons bomb shelter]] was constructed in the unlikely event Grievous or Dooku would try to destroy the [[Crispus Commons]] veteran facility on the planet [[Gorse]].[[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']] =====Last grasp===== [[File:Grievous-led-Outer-Rim-Sieges.png|thumb|right|300px|General Grievous orders the Separatist Army to besiege the Outer Rim, forcing the deployment of numerous Jedi Generals all around the Outer Rim.]] With the Separatists on the verge of losing the war, a major victory was required to break the Republic's will and the momentum of their attacks. Then, Dooku informed Grievous with the news that he was expecting; Darth Sidious had obtained the coordinates for Grievous and his fleet to leap from the Outer Rim directly to Coruscant, as well as a plan to kidnap the Supreme Chancellor. Grievous was given the opportunity to strike a decisive blow by moving the fight to the heart of the Republic. He headed to the galactic capital. While Coruscant remained well-defended, its fleet was depleted by the need to divert forces to the Outer Rim Sieges. To the Republic, a surprise attack seemed impossible with the Separatists occupied in the Outer Rim and the [[Nexus Route]] coordinates firmly locked away, preventing the Separatists from striking directly at the capital. However, by sharing the coordinates with Palpatine, the Jedi Order had unknowingly delivered the secret directly to their enemy.{{EncyclopediaCite|The End of the Clone Wars}} With a strike at Coruscant possible, the CIS had a chance to recover and emerge victorious. Gathering his forces for an attack on the Core's heart, Grievous thought that such an attack would cause the recall of Republic forces participating in the Outer Rim Sieges, therefore removing or at least rendering the blockades permeable. It was a risky gamble that, if successful, could signal the end of the conflict. Despite the pressure put upon the CIS and the losses it had sustained, Grievous marshalled his forces for a counterattack and began his own offensive across the Outer Rim. His counteroffensive pushed the Republic's forces outside the Core, already stretched across the Outer Rim in the Republic's own offensive,{{BustCollectionCite|31|Star Wars Universe}} to a breaking point. Forced out of the Core Worlds and spreading across the galaxy, the Jedi helped their beleaguered clones in an effort to defend against Grievous's attacks in what would amount to be the war's desperate, final hours. At one point during the sieges, Grievous was aboard the bridge of a starship, observing six Providence-class Dreadnoughts [[Battle between a Republic and Separatist fleet|attack]] a Republic fleet of at least six Venator-class Star Destroyers. Grievous was rumored to be [[Mission to Frong|possibly present]] on [[Frong]], one of the many planets in the Outer Rim that were under siege, and if he were, the general should be captured, and despite the Jedi Council's lack of evidence, it's clear that the Separatists are engaging in some sort of activity, and must find out what. ====Battle of Coruscant==== {{Quote|Your lightsabers will make a fine addition to my collection.|General Grievous|}} [[File:Grievous_on_Invisible_Hand.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous aboard the ''Invisible Hand''.]] With the Republic Military and Jedi busy with the Outer Rim Sieges raging across the galaxy's spiral arms, Coruscant was left with fewer defenses. With Republic strategists unworried, Sidious,{{Databank|palpatine-biography-gallery|Palpatine Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image 19 caption}} through Dooku, arranged for Grievous to launch a [[Battle of Coruscant|massive assault]] to capture his own alter ego, [[Supreme Chancellor]] Sheev Palpatine. The cyborg was charged with abducting the Chancellor and keeping him safe until the Jedi arrived to rescue him. Grievous, however, was entirely unaware of Palpatine's real identity. He took a dozen MagnaGuards as part of a large force to distract any Jedi during his escape. Dooku had earlier relocated his command post to Grievous's flagship, the ''Invisible Hand'', allowing him to be close to Grievous and ensure his orders were carried out, but even though a creature like the cyborg general posed no threat to the Sith Master, Sidious did not want any setbacks to his plans.{{EncyclopediaCite|Emperor Palpatine}} Grievous and his forces emerged from hyperspace with hundreds upon hundreds of C-9979 landing craft and thousands upon thousands of their Vulture droid and [[Droid tri-fighter]] escorts swept past toward the planet's surface and opened fire on the fleet of ships guarding Coruscant, wreaking destruction on the planet. The [[Coruscant Home Defense Fleet]] was caught off guard, and, with the chaos and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems Navy|Confederacy navy]] providing cover, Grievous and a strike team could land on Coruscant's surface. Within minutes, a significant number of Republic Star Destroyers protecting the [[Ecumenopolis|cityworld]] were reduced to fiery rubble, with the ''Invisible Hand'' accounting for a large percentage of the deaths. In space, Droid tri-fighters quickly decimated Republic [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter|ARC-170 fighter]] squadrons, while droid fighters flying to the battle on the surface supported the battle droids with their passes, spraying enemies on the ground with fire, immobilizing Jedi Masters Yoda and Mace Windu long enough for Grievous to act. Amidst the chaos and panic, Dooku remained in orbit and directed the aerial attack on Coruscant,{{BustCollectionCite|37|Star Wars Universe}} while Grievous flew down to the planet itself and landed in the [[Federal District|Executive District]], commanding an armed force, carried out the ground raid, and then appeared in [[Palpatine's apartment]], accompanied by his electrostaff-equipped MagnaGuards. Despite Shaak Ti and Corobb's best efforts to get Palpatine to safety, Grievous fought his way through layers of Republic security forces, including clone troopers and Jedi protectors, to secure Palpatine, eliminating everyone either by subduing or killing them, killing Jedi Master [[Roron Corobb]], whose lightsaber he claimed, during his hunt for Palpatine. During the defense, Kit Fisto attempted to defend the Chancellor from Grievous. Last but not least, he also incapacitated Ti using electrified cables, knocking her unconscious and claiming her weapon as well. He then took a single, but invaluable prisoner, the Chancellor, and carried him away{{EncyclopediaCite|Padmé Amidala}} aboard his flagship, the ''Invisible Hand'', leading him to the still-waiting Dooku in [[Conning tower|Communications tower]], where Dooku took charge of keeping Palpatine captive. Grievous was also warned by Dooku that the Jedi would stage a rescue mission. Grievous had already captured Palpatine and returned to his flagship by the time the Coruscant Home Fleet had finally established assault positions. Before Grievous could escape into hyperspace with the captured Chancellor, Republic reinforcements arrived into the battle with the ''Invisible Hand'' as their main target. While the Home Fleet moved to prevent Grievous from reaching a jump point from which the Separatist leaders could escape, thus keeping the ''Invisible Hands'' in the midst of the battle, a rescue squad under Kenobi and Skywalker, who had rushed to Coruscant from the planet [[Yerbana]] upon learning of Grievous's attack, raced to board the ''Invisible Hand'' while Commander [[Honor Salima]] of the Home Fleet rallied her vessels to stop the Separatists from escaping or disengaging. Amid the slugging match that the battle devolved into, Kenobi, Skywalker, and [[Clone Flight Squad Seven]] raced forward despite squadrons of droid fighters confronting them, resulting in many of the clone pilots being shot down. However, the two Jedi managed to board the ''Invisible Hand'' and race toward its Conning tower to save Palpatine. Upon returning to the bridge, Grievous was informed of the Jedi incursion by his Neimoidian captain [[Lushros Dofine]], but the cyborg merely laughed at how Dooku's prediction had come true. [[File:FirstDate-ROTS.png|thumb|right|300px|Much to Grievous's delight, he was met face-to-face with a captured Anakin Skywalker and his old enemy Obi-Wan Kenobi.]] Fighting past the battle droids who tried to stop them, the two Jedi, accompanied by R2-D2, made it to the [[Observation deck|observation platform]] atop the towering spire where Palpatine was being held, and upon their arrival, rather than Grievous, they were confronted by Dooku, whose presence proved to be fortunate for the Republic; the two clashed with Dooku until Skywalker bested the Separatist Head of State and killed on Palpatine's orders. His death was a major blow to the CIS. Meanwhile, the ''Invisible Hand'' was surrounded by [[Home Fleet Strike Group Five]] under [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Lorth Needa]] and demanded the Kaleesh surrender. Needa did not believe Grievous's claims that Palpatine was a prisoner on board. Although he gave the cyborg ten minutes to prove himself before his ships opened fire, Grievous did not surrender.{{BuildFalconCite|52|Starship Fact File}} Informed by one of his OOM pilots that they had located the Jedi in [[Hallway 328]], Grievous had them trapped within a [[ray shield]] and escorted to the bridge by droids. In a moment that filled Grievous with satisfaction, Obi-Wan and Anakin were marched onto his bridge in [[Stuncuffs|electrobonds]]. The ''Invisible Hand'' began to weaken to the punishment it was receiving as Grievous captured Obi-Wan, Skywalker, and Palpatine. An [[OOM command battle droid]] handed Kenobi and [[Skywalker lightsaber|Skywalker's lightsabers]] to Grievous, who took them and weighed them in his metal claws. According to the Jedi, constructing their own lightsaber was not simply a weapon but also a piece of art that perfectly reflected its owner. A comprehensive analysis of the lightsaber could reveal much about the Jedi who made it, but there would be time for that later. Turning to face his prisoners, Grievous expanded to his full height. He enjoyed looking down on them, the terror in their eyes as they wondered what awful weapons were behind his long cloak, and the fear as they stared up at his expressionless metal face. Nonetheless, the Jedi appeared underwhelmed; Grievous would change that. Grievous and Anakin Skywalker finally meet face-to-face, both mocking one another, with Skywalker angering him in the process. He swept his cape back, revealing the lightsabers hanging in its lining, boasting that their lightsabers would make an excellent addition to his collection. [[File:Grievous-is-surrounded.png|thumb|left|250px|Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi corner Grievous who prepares to shatter the viewport before him to escape.]] Still unaware that Dooku had been killed on the observation deck, Grievous was delighted to have captured his old adversary Kenobi and the legendary Skywalker and celebrated his victory and secretly reveled in having total control over the entire fleet when he was briefly distracted by Skywalker's droid, R2-D2. As planned, the Jedi launched a surprise escape; Obi-Wan retrieved his lightsaber back from him, escaped his bond, and freed Anakin. Grievous stepped away, placing his bodyguards between him and the free Jedi. Standing back-to-back, the two Jedi deflected blaster fire from the surrounding droids. Some of his crew members had been struck by blaster shots, and he wasn't about to suffer the same fate. Thus, he let the droids exhaust the Jedi and approached one of the ship's pilots and ordered them not to deal with them and to keep the ship in orbit. The chancellor was dragged to safety by the battle droids, as the Jedi took on the task of dealing with the general's bodyguards. Obi-Wan and Anakin, now accustomed to dealing with even [[phrik]] alloy electrostaff-wielding MagnaGuards, destroyed [[IG-101]] and [[IG-102]], leaving them free to corner Grievous. The ship's [[Artificial gravity generator|gravity grids]] altered, and suddenly the ceiling was below. Most of the battle droids fell to the ceiling with the Jedi, but few of them reacted in time to stick to the floor. With that, the Jedi destroyed a handful of them. A Neimoidian pilot, in terror, announces that the ship is disaggregating. Grievous saw that staying to win this fight was pointless, therefore letting the Jedi dissolve with the ship. The [[gravity]] unexpectedly returns to normal as the Jedi fall back to the ground and sprint in the direction of the Kaleesh general. Almost all of the droids were out of order. The Supreme Chancellor was quickly saved for the second time, and Grievous was trapped on his own bridge. With his leader dead and bodyguards gone, Grievous knew the odds were against him. The Jedi clearly had the upper hand and managed to hurt the general. Reconsidering his plan, the general declared that Kenobi had lost and shattered the front window of the cruiser with an electrostaff. The cyborg was dragged into space as the compressed air inside the ship rushed into the vacuum, while Obi-Wan and Anakin fought not to follow him. Kenobi, Skywalker and the Chancellor managed to stay in the ship, but Grievous was sucked into space. Using a [[grappling hook]] built into his arm and his clawed feet to latch onto the hull of the ship, Grievous climbed back onboard the ship to reach the escape pods. As he moved along the smooth metal, he remarked to himself how easy it was to have a droid body. [[File:Grievous_escape_pod.png|thumb|right|250px|With his ship lost, Grievous was forced to escape to save his life, using one of the escape pods.]] Leaving everyone on board, the Separatist commander launched all of the escape pods, took off in one, and rapidly moved away from the remnant of his flagship. Grievous usually finds himself an escape route, but as the Battle of Coruscant took place, he was alone without the ''Soulless One''. He would have lost it along with his flagship, the ''Invisible Hand'', if this had happened. By that time, the starfighter had been on a small landing platform on Utapau for several months. Anakin and Obi-Wan discovered that he had survived by doubling back by this. The Trade Federation shuttles were close enough to pick him up, and the clone fighters were too preoccupied with battling his droids to pay him any attention. Grievous's escape pod was recovered by the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk-class Battleship'']] ''[[Profusion]]'', and rejoined his fleet. With Palpatine out of his grasp, Grievous ordered his forces to flee and led the two-thirds of his armada capable of fleeing into hyperspace. ====Retreat to Utapau==== {{Quote|The end of the war is near, general.''"
"''But the loss of Count Dooku?''"
"''His death was a necessary loss. Soon I will have a new apprentice, one far younger and more powerful.|Sidious and Grievous|}} With a full third of the Separatist fleet used in the battle over Coruscant having suffered major damages, much of the navy was decimated and could not follow Grievous to safety. In the aftermath, Republic military officers analyzed the battle's footage in an attempt to identify the Separatist strategy and the reason they had remained in the system for so long after capturing Palpatine. Unaware that Dooku's escape was never his intention; Palpatine used the battle entirely as bait to bring Anakin Skywalker back to Coruscant, eliminate Dooku, and prepare the Republic for its dying days. Following Dooku's unexpected death,{{Topps|set=2017 Topps Journey to Star Wars: The Last Jedi|cardname=Confronting General Grievous}} which struck a major blow to the Separatist cause and the Separatists' hopes, Grievous succeeded him as [[Head of State]], turning the Supreme Commander into the leader of the entire Separatist Alliance. While Grievous had always been in command of the droid army,''[[Skywalker: A Family at War]]'' his promotion left him with complete control over Separatist forces as both the military and political head. Despite the usefulness of such a promotion, Grievous remained subservient to Sidious, whom he continued to loyally serve. After the Jedi Knights foiled his plan to kidnap Chancellor Palpatine, Grievous fled to the Outer Rim and ordered a brutal, but clearly desperate, counterattack across several [[star system]]s, including Kaller,{{TBB|Aftermath (episode)}} even though the CIS had largely been forced on the defensive as the Outer Rim Sieges continued. Despite being used in his counterattack, the legions of battle droids Grievous could command were severely depleted, whereas the Republic was securing more and more victories across the galaxy. Grievous, ever the faithful servant to Sidious, was now ordered to return to Utapau in the Outer Rim and safeguard the security the increasingly irrelevant Separatist Council. In reality, Sidious had other plans for Grievous, who failed to realize he was being tricked again. The cyborg had one role left to play in the Sith Lord's schemes: to act as bait to draw Kenobi away from Coruscant and Anakin Skywalker. With his Grand Plan to bring down the Republic and Jedi Order in motion, Darth Sidious did not care if Grievous or Kenobi lived or died. [[File:Grievous-speaks-to-Sidious.png|thumb|left|254px|Grievous was assured by Darth Sidious that the war was coming to an end and that the Separatists would be victorious.]] Grievous particularly disliked Utapau, a planet where he had been humiliated by Kenobi and Skywalker during the kyber crystal endeavor, and regarded its people as wretched worms.''[[Revenge of the Sith - The Film Novel]]'' All the same, Grievous traveled aboard his personal{{BuildFalconCite|54|Starship Fact File}} [[Unidentified Sheathipede-class transport shuttle (Grievous)|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttle]] to the planet for his meeting with the Separatist Council, and he had returned in some force, deriving some satisfaction by taking the Pau'un leaders hostage and beginning to transform their capital into a droid factory. Grievous had taken over a major portion of the city and held the populace hostage, threatening them with fiery destruction if they revealed his presence there. When Grievous arrived, his droids informed him that the planet is under his command. [[File:Kenobi_faces_Grievous_ROTS.png|thumb|left|264px|On Utapau, Grievous faces Obi-Wan Kenobi, his great adversary, for the last time.]] Unknowingly, however, Grievous had played directly into Kenobi's hands as the Jedi General waited for Cody and the 212th to arrive. [[File:Obi-WanclasheswithGrievous.png|thumb|right|264px|During their duel, despite having four lightsabers, Grievous quickly loses two hands to Kenobi's blade.]] Grievous was driven back further and further by Obi-Wan, who maintained the lead as the surrounding droids watched as their leader lost ground.
