Often donned with a Kaleesh mask sculpted from the skull of a Mumuu, a hostile predator native to his homeworld of Kalee, Grievous wore the mask throughout the duration of his people's war with the Huk. With a desire to become the leader of the largest and greatest military force within the entire galaxy, as well as possess the capability to combat Jedi, whom he had perceived as nearly invincible as a result of their powerful connection to the Force, the Kaleesh also aspired to become a great warrior and gained the reputation of an infamous warlord who developed vast numbers of enemies. When transformed into a reconstructed cybernetic warrior following his decision to embark on such a path and a gruesome shuttle crash, Grievous's brain was altered by Separatist engineers without conscience by the Kaleesh, which resulted in an increase in intelligence, agility and strength, as well as a deep and violent disposition for the Jedi following the false revelation by Count Dooku that the Jedi were responsible for his condition. As a result, Grievous was tall, and his metal-plate body resembled the form of a mechanical skeleton, similar to armor but welded together with no room for flesh. In almost any meeting, it was a powerful presence that could intimidate others. With his cybernetic transformation, Grievous exuded a malevolent demeanor.{{InsiderCite|231|Launchpad}} He received claw-like feet, a set of arms which were capable of separating themselves into an additional set, and a skull-like Kaleesh mask that had been specifically sculpted for his new body, from which his eyes peered through. revealing his being's cyborg nature. Furthermore, located behind a set of duranium teeth crafted to mimic those of the karabbac beast from his homeworld, Grievous's hoarse voice was emitted from an ultrasonic vocabulator. Grievous's magnetized talons were made of durasteel. ===General of the Confederacy=== {{Quote|Listen to me, Jedi. I do not care about your politics. I do not care about your Republic. I only live to see you die!|General Grievous's message to the Jedi Order|}} Alongside a hatred for political matters, Grievous had developed an understanding that his involvement in the Clone Wars was an opportunity to eliminate the Jedi Order and command the Separatist Droid Army, as opposed to serving Dooku's political ambitions. However, as a result of his preeminent desire to eradicate the Jedi, many within the Confederacy, such as General Kleeve, considered his personal goals as a distraction which prevented his successes in the war. Grievous was regarded by Maul as having a narrow perspective and lacked the plans and ambitions that he and Dooku had. Although the general himself lacked a sense of humor and found pleasure in murder, he was able to prioritize his responsibilities. He was quite proud of his position within the Separatist organizations and told others to refer to him as "general". He was also referred to as "My [[lord]]" by members of the Confederacy military, such as Asajj Ventress and TV-94. [[File:ChokedCloneTrooper-BFR.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous was a ruthless adversary who killed the strong and the helpless alike.]] Grievous was known for his cruelty and ruthlessness and was seen as the Separatists' best general. Given his reputation, Grievous was feared throughout the galaxy as a strategic genius and for his hunting prowess.{{SW|url=news/sdcc-2019-marvels-the-rise-of-kylo-ren-revealed-and-more-highlights-from-the-lucasfilm-publishing-panel|text=SDCC 2019: Marvel's ''The Rise of Kylo Ren'' Revealed and More Highlights from the Lucasfilm Publishing Panel}} Following Count Dooku, General Grievous was viewed by the Republic as the second biggest threat in the war. The Republic described Grievous as a mechanical monstrosity, a portrayal that appealed to deep-seated droid anxieties. No one terrorizes Republic soldiers more than Grievous, the fearsome combatant of the Clone Wars, both as a strategic mind and a battlefield nightmare. Whether setting his army against entire worlds or facing opponents in close-up and lethal combat, Grievous was a symbol of terror throughout the galaxy. The Jedi Knights felt hatred and fear for Grievous, but not everyone felt the same way. For example, [[Thirteenth Sister|Iskat Akaris]] was fascinated by him and dreamed of fighting him. According to legend, even the Jedi shuddered when his name was mentioned and feared meeting him in battle, as none could match his sheer relentlessness and determination. Behind Grievous's mask lurks one of the era's shrewdest military strategists, one who isn't afraid to retreat if the odds were stacked against him. If he was outmatched, Grievous preferred short battles and continuous retreats, realizing it was best to survive and regularly avoiding capture by the Republic, slipping away to fight another day, and constantly frustrating Republic commanders who sought his capture or death. However, Grievous has been persuaded by the CIS's limited and unreliable resources to see the need for a quick and trustworthy evacuation strategy on even the safest of postings. He regards withdrawal as more of a setback than denying the Republic complete triumph. Grievous's military legend as a cunning wrath who plunged in and out of engagements secretly and quickly was a powerful weapon in the arsenal of the Separatists, and his own starfighter was a continuation of that standing. While the general had a reputation among Republic and Jedi circles for retreating, his direct superiors respected his careful and clever tactical decisions.{{BuildFalconCite|40|Starship Fact File}} The brutal strategy he learned as a warlord required the Jedi to command clone troopers, which are made through technological advances. Many of the Jedi Council recognized the dangers to the Order, but they were pressured by the next incursion or the next loss of a world to the cyborg Separatist Leader. Another outlined in the legend of the Battle of Alamass, Separatist leaders believed Grievous could be relied upon to complete critical missions, for his record was nearly unblemished and he was highly regarded for his tactical insight, which provided the Separatists with numerous victories. While Dooku dealt with matters of state, including military operations for the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Grievous supervised the logistics and tactics of its vast droid armies, supervised by Dooku's operatives, and handled the war's day-to-day operations. The general oversaw a large number of capable admirals and generals recruited from across the Galaxy. Grievous, Trench, and their fellow commanders were placed in charge of the broader campaign objectives, whereas Asajj Ventress employed stealth, bribery, robbery, and targeted killing to achieve her finer goals. Grievous's campaigns against the Galactic Republic threatened the very existence of the Jedi Order. He could impose better control over his forces, thanks to the droid commanders who eliminated the unauthorized thoughts and suggestions from underlings with internal strategic prowess. Only a few brilliant sentients, such as Admiral Trench, managed to stay in charge of offensive operations. In contrast, local forces, frequently organic, are primarily responsible for defensive actions, allowing the locals to protect and strengthen their homeworld and hyperspace passages, leaving Grievous to concentrate on assaulting the Republic. ===Cyborg tyrant=== {{Quote|Those of you who can still stand— Return to your master…''and tell him to send more men!''|Grievous, upon slaughtering several Mandalorian warriors|}} [[File:GrievousRevealsHimselfMygeeto-Kanan10.png|thumb|left|250px|A cyborg warrior who did not need the Force to confront Jedi, Grievous struck fear in the hearts of those who supported the Republic.]] Cold, calculating, vain,{{Databank|general-grievous-speeder|General Grievous' Speeder}} deceitful, and unconcerned with the rules of combat outlined by the Galactic Accord of Systems, his cruelty was not limited to the field of battle. Civilians and other non-combatants suffered, with Grievous devastating the populations of entire worlds. His tactic was to exploit the compassion of his foes, targeting civilians and forcing his opponents to priorities the protection of innocents. This left his troops to focus on victory at any cost. The general was aware of the Jedi's soft spot for innocents and did not care himself about civilian casualties, exploiting the Jedi compassion for civilians and the clone troopers under their command. Grievous enjoyed a good conquest. Dooku considered Grievous a successful leader due to the cyborg's ability to see the big picture; the general carried out high-handed tactics such as employing listening sites to ambush Republic fleets and attempting to invade Kamino to stop clone production.{{InsiderCite|188|The Grievous Growl}} He was never thrilled to receive orders and truly despised being paired with other commanders, believing it to be an insult on his ability as a leader and warrior. Though Grievous felt that he would emerge victorious, he was also arrogant enough to dismiss his subordinates' recommendations for caution. Although he had his own personal starfighter, Grievous was more frequently seen as commander of a capital-class vessel. He frequently commands naval engagements from his flagship dreadnought, the ''Invisible Hand'', demonstrating that becoming a cyborg had not lessened his tactical talents, but his combat, experience, and brutality shine in hand-to-hand combat. Throughout the war, Grievous utilizes his agile fleets to strike planets like Falleen and Dorin, disrupting the Republic. Unable to predict where the droid general will strike next, the Republic became distracted, leaving previously conquered worlds open to Separatist control. In command of a huge droid army, largest ever created, Grievous committed blunders, although his losses were frequently only brief. He did experience defeats, however, and lost his first command ship, the ''Malevolence'', to the efforts of Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi, two Jedi who would continue to be a source of pain for him. Playing an active role in the war, Grievous was often leading troops from the front in a horrifying display of lightsaber prowess and mechanical body strength, utilizing his enhanced physical capabilities to attack opposing forces, crushing everyone who came in reach, including Jedi. He prefers the front lines, surrounded by IG-100 MagnaGuards, and challenges Jedi Generals in hopes of adding their lightsabers to his collection. [[File:BattleOfDathomir-Sisters.png|thumb|right|300px|General Grievous was a ruthless warrior who waged and led campaigns of destruction and devastation.]] Not only was General Grievous a callously brilliant strategist, but his own skills as a warrior made him a deadly opponent in his own right. The general demonstrated that one need not be strong in the Force to threaten even the greatest Jedi in combat. He considers himself a superior warrior, believing his mechanical limbs have made him superior to all opponents, and sought to prove himself in combat. On the battlefield, Grievous could be heard nursing a brutal hacking cough.{{Topps|set= 2018 Topps Star Wars: The Clone Wars 10th Anniversary|cardname=General Grievous}} Even with this drawback, he proved to be the most fearsome of opponents, with his whole, fast-moving physique best described as a living weapon.{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|cardname=General Grievous}} One of Grievous's weaknesses was that he failed to see how superior his enhanced cyborg abilities were to the slow-thinking droids under his commands. He had little understanding of the Force, though he believed that the improvements made to his body gave him a greater power than that of the Jedi he hunted. He replaced this gap of knowledge with an appetite for destruction, especially of the power he did not truly comprehend. However, transforming his body into a fighting machine left Grievous's organic anatomy weak inside his armor. Grievous's hatred for the Jedi was well known throughout the galaxy and was stated by him on many occasions. A feared Jedi hunter, he was well known for his brutality and ruthlessness. He savored each slaughter he made, especially those of children, and took morbid satisfaction in thrashing Jedi on the battlefield and pursuing down nimble Jedi, something he thoroughly enjoyed doing. While a fearsome warrior, he was known to be quick to run from a fight when the tide was turned against him, frequently scuttling away to safety using all four limbs. This tactic worked, until his final encounter with his nemesis, Jedi master Obi-Wan Kenobi, with whom Grievous shared a fierce rivalry. Kenobi could recognize the cyborg's mechanical cough from anywhere. The Jedi considered such devious tactics to be cowardly, but Grievous held no notions of honor. Though Mace Windu and the rest of the Council branded Grievous a coward, running and hiding, as he has always done, despite not being able to wield the Force, the truth was that he was a relentless and expert opponent who had defeated numerous Jedi in battle. Grievous has a brooding and sarcastic personality,{{EncyclopediaCite|Protocol and Service Droids}} showed sadism, and known for being just as callous as the droids he commands, whom he believes to be wrong. Grievous utilized Jedi Master Eeth Koth to express fear and anguish, knowing that Koth's suffering would pain the Jedi Order via the Force. The cyborg had a vicious tendency of killing Jedi out of retaliation then keeping their lightsabers as trophies and enjoyed utilizing them in battle. When Kenobi and Skywalker were brought into his custody on the ''Invisible Hand'', the satisfied Grievous would have smiled if it was possible for him. Grievous had supreme confidence in his own abilities, and was often arrogant, believing himself to be untouchable. Grievous also insisted on fighting Jedi personally whenever possible, even when injured, which betrayed a sense of recklessness and restlessness in the cyborg general. This was shown by his refusal to heed EV-A4D's advice to recuperate after his first bout with Kit Fisto and his former apprentice Nahdar Vebb. He acted recklessly again when he fought Obi-Wan on Utapau that proved to be his undoing. ===Vicious streak and beyond the Jedi=== {{Quote|Whenever Grievous or Ventress cut down a Jedi, they brought me these little souvenirs of the battle. They make for quite the handsome display, don't you think?|Dooku, to Quinlan Vos|}} [[File:GrievousSaberCollection-ROTS.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous had a reputation for killing Jedi and taking their lightsabers as trophies.]] In a gloomy trophy room within his secret fortress, Grievous kept a collection of his victims' weapons and proudly displayed his expanding collection of war trophies that had started when he was still a warlord on Kalee, the lightsabers of his defeated enemies, and other souvenirs, such as a horrific case of severed [[Padawan braid|Padawan's braids]] struck down before their [[Knighting Ceremony|knighting]]. Grievous carried many stolen lightsabers in the lining of his cape or on his waist to terrify all challengers. By the end of the Clone Wars, he had nearly a hundred in his macabre collection, and he had been rumored to have captured or killed dozens of Jedi, including Jedi Master Neebo and the recently knighted Nahdar Vebb. In specific, he found great pleasure in hunting Jedi and claiming their lightsabers as trophies. Both Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi were able to avoid being added to Grievous's victim list. Although Grievous killed many Jedi during the Clone Wars, his greatest prizes were the lightsabers of Pablo-Jill, Eeth Koth, Roron Corobb, and Shaak Ti. Nahdar Vebb's lightsaber was briefly a part of his collection but was lost when Kit Fisto reclaimed it. At one point, Grievous gained the lightsaber of Jedi Master Jmmaar.[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] His ruthless streak stretched beyond the Jedi, as he personally killed Gungan General Roos Tarpals on Naboo and massacred the Nightsisters of Dathomir, where he showed no mercy and wiped out an [[Dathomiri clan|entire clan]] of witches, including one of the oldest and wisest Nightsisters,{{SWE|characters|olddaka|Old Daka}} Old Daka, leaving just a few Nightsisters alive. He was also given the honor of killing the defeated Mother Talzin, a powerful elder [[matriarch]] who had escaped his wrath before. ===Relationships=== {{Quote|Chancellor Palpatine managed to escape your grip, general. Without Count Dooku, I have doubts about your ability to keep us safe.''"
"''Be thankful, Viceroy, you have not found yourself in my grip.|Nute Gunray, and Grievous' retort|}} [[File:Grievous_SOM.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous conferring with Dooku.]] Grievous was loyal to both of his masters, Count Dooku and Darth Sidious, While Grievous had clashes with Dooku, he displayed a great respect towards the Confederacy's leader, whose orders the general would carry out without hesitation. Indeed, Grievous once made it clear to [[Nix Card]] that Dooku was the only person he was willing to take orders from, although he was also more than willing to obey the whims of the shadowy Sidious. Dooku himself, however, regarded the cyborg as nothing more than a useful tool.{{Databank|url=count-dooku-biography-gallery|title=Count Dooku Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image caption 11}} He shared his master's confidence, such as when Dooku informed him of Savage Opress's growing power, to which Grievous simply laughed at the notion that Opress could pose a threat to them. Grievous believes that Dooku was a former student trained by Jedi Master Yoda. After Maul and Mother Talzin successfully captured Dooku, Grievous was trusted enough to join Sidious in rescuing him from a Nightbrother village on Dathomir. For all the respect he showed Dooku, such as directly calling the count his master, Grievous also had a hate for Dooku, which deepened when Dooku leaked the location of his lair to the Jedi, something that Grievous was unwilling to forgive. While fleeing the Battle of Coruscant, Grievous decided that, with any luck, he would be able to blame the disaster on Dooku. Furthermore, Grievous expressed no remorse for the count's death at the hands of Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, even if Dooku had helped him in lightsaber combat; rather, he viewed having full control over the Separatist forces as immensely helpful. Grievous knew that Darth Sidious was Count Dooku's master, but he had no idea that he was actually Sheev Palpatine himself. In a meeting with Sidious and other Separatists, Grievous learned of a new and even more powerful "apprentice" but never learned of their identity.[[Star Wars Jedi Master Magazine 3|''Star Wars Jedi Master'' Magazine 3]] While Sidious had no need for the cyborg by that time and abandoned his pawn, Grievous sought to show himself worthy of Sidious. [[File:VentressFlirty-ARCTroopers.png|thumb|left|278x278px|Ventress teases Grievous on Kamino.]] Despite being on the same side,{{EncyclopediaCite|Boba Fett and Other Characters of the Underworld}} General Grievous and Asajj Ventress shared a rivalry, and this suited Count Dooku perfectly and was very much the Sith way. There was an implication of perpetual conflict between them demonstrated by how both worked separately, rather than together. Grievous and Ventress were constantly tested and challenged by Dooku, in the same way Dooku's master repeatedly tested and challenged him. Grievous seemed to hold a little respect for her, as he praised her on her style and noted that they could be equals, but Ventress dismissed the idea. Unaware that it was Dooku who had turned on Ventress, Grievous regarded her as a traitor after her departure from the CIS. The general openly declared that he had always been superior to her during the Battle of Dathomir. Grievous and Ventress shared some traits; neither had a deep affection for the Jedi Order and both disliked battle droids. As for Grievous, the Republic and the Jedi intervened in a conflict between his people and the Huk, siding with their enemy and leaving his people to starve to death; as for Ventress, the Jedi had abandoned''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]'' her master, [[Ky Narec]], who had discovered her on the planet [[Rattatak]]{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}} and taught her in the use of the Force. Grievous has some regard for others patriotism. Grievous had always disliked Nute Gunray, the Neimoidian Viceroy who led the Separatist Council, Gunray, in turn, despised Grievous for Count Dooku preferential treatment of the cyborg. He threatened to kill Gunray, when the Neimoidian was brave enough to publicly criticize the cyborg. Gor was one of the few creatures that Grievous cared for, displaying a certain affection for his cyborg pet and being dismayed upon learning of the creature's death, which became another reason for his hatred of the Jedi. He also developed a kind of bond with his medical droid EV-A4-D, though he yelled at him from time to time and humiliated him, he let him criticize him without tearing him apart. Grievous shared his secrets with his medical droid, one of the few entitles in the galaxy who knew Grievous's secrets.{{BuildR2Cite|20|Droid Directory}} [[File:ScuttlingtoSafety-GeneralGrievous-SWU.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Grievous had a low opinion of his B1 battle droids.]] Despite commanding the Separatists' droid armies, Grievous also had a disdain and lack of regard for the battle droids, especially B1 models, considering them all but useless, and was not hesitant to express his frustrations on nearby units and wouldn't hesitate to destroy or abandon them in an instant. Grievous was frequently dissatisfied with the droid army's failure to fulfill his strict standards and was one of many Separatist commanders who became upset by the droid's limitations.{{SW|url=battle-droid-history-gallery|text=Battle Droid History Gallery}} {{C|Image caption 14}} After suffering a humiliating defeat, distracting Grievous wielding a lightsaber in a bad mood never worked out well for the battle droid. Nonetheless, he was proud to lead what he believed to be the most powerful droid army the galaxy had ever seen. Legend claimed he was so willing to harm them because, in some ways, the droids reminded him of his own flaws. Furthermore, Grievous could not see the similarities between himself and the droids he harassed, believing that his organic heart made him stronger and better than the droids he tried to think he was nothing like. This habit often caused Dooku to remind Grievous that the droids were expensive and that they were made to follow orders, not question them. Considering the general's hatred of battle droids, his IG-100 MagnaGuards had to be impressively tough to survive his demands. He outfitted them with Kaleesh cloaks and head wraps echoed the outfits worn by his companions as a tribute. He volunteered to teach his MagnaGuards a variety of lessons on not only combat but also the psychology of living organic beings. With his four arms, smooth skull-like metal mask, and clawed feet, Grievous looked like something from a [[Dream|nightmare]] caused by the [[spice]], instead of looking like a real individual. He was more machine than living creature, but the amber slitted eyes that peered through his mask, staring down at opponents, revealed a dreadful malice: underneath the armor was the heart of an warlord,''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Head-to-Head]]'' who was regarded as an evil individual by his foes. Despite his tremendous power and having seemed like a mechanical creature on the exterior, Grievous felt humiliated and detested droids and responded violently if anybody dared to initially mistake him for a mere machine. Nonetheless, Grievous realized that his new form made him frightening and was concerned about his upgrades, insisting to EV-A4-D that they are "improvements." Legend specified in order to enjoy the benefits of both organic and inorganic lifeforms, he believed he could be as strong and versatile as a droid, with all the cunning, passion, and capacity for emotion of an organic being. On Utapau, it was not the first time he gloated over how his metal mask revealed no emotion, which was useful for Grievous when dealing with the Separatist Council; Grievous regarded them as ignorant beings who could not realize the extent of his disdain for them. [[File:GrievousBeforeCyborg-AORGrievous1.png|thumb|left|268x268px|Grievous feigned boastful satisfaction with his cybernetic form but was secretly angry.]] The legend of the Battle of Alamass made further claims about Grievous's mental state; despite his military prowess, the general was still unhappy, for though he changed his body, he was not satisfied with his fate in life. In truth, he would never find peace or completion in the continued modification of his form, for deep down he sought escape, and no matter how much he might change what he was, he could never change who he was. Being a creature who was ruled by his heart, however, the general could never see that in himself. As a result, the general who would become a cyborg was a troubled soul, and he expressed his troubles by the only means he knew how-violence. Grievous became angrier and more vengeful he became, lashing out at anybody he thought was weak. The pathological hatred he felt toward the Jedi, against whom he had sworn to exact a terrible vengeance for crimes against him and his people, caused Grievous to target Jedi one by one. After the catastrophic intervention of the Galactic Republic and Jedi in a conflict between his people and the Huk decades earlier, Grievous believed it is his duty to rid the galaxy of Jedi "filth." By the time of the Clone Wars, Grievous cared not for the Republic or any political motivation to fight and instead focused his energy on destroying the Jedi Order. ==Skills and abilities== ===Lightsaber abilities=== {{Quote|You fool! I've been trained in your Jedi arts by Count Dooku!|Grievous to Obi-Wan Kenobi|}} [[File:AoR-GeneralGrievous-Larraz-textless.png|thumb|right|200x320px|Grievous was very skilled with lightsabers, which allowed him to defeat and kill several great Jedi duelists.]] Although he lacked a powerful connection to the Force, Grievous was a highly skilled warrior who was capable of proficiently wielding lightsabers in combat against his enemies. His skill was a result of training received from Count Dooku, a Sith Lord once a Jedi Master. As the Separatist cyborg did not use the Force, Grievous' stolen lightsabers lacked the dark-side-induced corruption necessary for his [[bleeding|kyber to bleed]] and glowed the same color as those of the former masters he had slain. A master of several forms of lightsaber combat, Grievous was capable of quickly adapting to the fighting styles implemented by his opponents. Furthermore, due to the enhancements provided to him by his cybernetics, the Kaleesh often utilized superior strength and agility during his encounters with Jedi. A skilled lightsaber combatant who specialized in the form known as [[Jar'Kai]], which contributed to his personalized style of combat, Grievous utilized the advantage of his additional limbs during battle with others, which thereby allowed him to wield four lightsabers as a result and employ a personalized variation to overwhelm opponents. His strategy dictated that the three key elements of fear, surprise, and intimidation were needed to undermine an enemy's abilities; if any of these were absent, it would be preferable to withdraw and reestablish them. Throughout the duration of the Clone Wars as a cyborg warrior, Grievous often clashed blades with numerous Jedi Generals of the Republic. His blade killed numerous Jedi that came into contact with him, and indeed surviving an encounter with Grievous was something that few Jedi could accomplish.{{HelmetCollectionCite|19|Databank A-Z}} Even members of the Jedi Council struggled to challenge him. Grievous could destroy numerous enemies, including clone troopers, droids, Gungans, and Mandalorian warriors. He also was able to battle and defeat, or at least hold his own against, members of the Jedi Order, such as the wise and tactical Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi on several occasions throughout much of the Clone Wars to a stalemate or an interruption, including a duel on Caliban; onboard the Subjugator-class cruiser, the ''Malevolence''; aboard the cruiser ''[[Surrogator]]'' in the Saleucami system; on Kamino; and aboard Kenobi's command ship, the Negotiator, near Florrum. Against Jedi Master Kit Fisto, although he lost one hand, he still held his own against the Nautolan Jedi to a standstill until the MagnaGuards showed up and surrounded him. Then, against Eeth Koth, Grievous was able to push Koth back, although he then used his MagnaGuards to subdue him. Grievous engaged Master Adi Gallia on two occasions; aboard the ''Surrogator'', the two briefly dueled, but Grievous managed to escape, and aboard her flagship, Grievous fought Gallia in the middle of a firefight, during which he sent her flying with a kick, defeating and seizing her as a prisoner. According to the Kaleesh general’s own account, he once braved the entire Jedi strike team. Grievous quickly overpowered Ahsoka Tano, the Padawan of Anakin Skywalker, in their first encounter during their time aboard Skytop Station, knocking her unconscious in the process, where he utilized intimidation tactics, such as roaring, to discourage his opponent. However, while Tano had improved by the time of their second encounter on the planet Florrum, as she utilized the Force to gain an advantage, Grievous was once again able to overpower the Padawan through the implementation of his additional limbs and clawed feet. The general almost defeated Kenobi several times, successfully defeated him onboard the ''Negotiator'' near Florrum and Separatist supply ship above Utapau, but was later slain on that same planet by the Jedi. Although the Grand Jedi Master's Force abilities proving too much for the general to handle, Grievous was capable of going toe-to-toe against Yoda on his own. Grievous fought Depa Billaba in at least two different duels; on Haruun Kal, he caused serious injuries to Billaba, leaving her in a six-month coma; on Myeeto, although he lost two upper hands, Grievous landed a glancing blow behind her back and still able to hold his own. During his mission to capture the Chancellor, Grievous dueled Shaak Ti; Ti managed to fight further, but Grievous managed to get the upper hand. He ensnared her with electrified cables, which knocked her unconscious. [[File:2ndBattleDathomir-SoD-4.png|thumb|left|280px|Grievous could encounter Jedi Order members, whom he was known to despise, but he could also face off against others.]] Although Grievous usually encountered members of the Jedi Order he despised, he could also face off against non-members. According to the legend, Grievous could face even the most fearsome opponents without worrying about pain or suffering injuries or having to hold back in his attack out of concern for vengeance, as damaged droid parts could be easily repaired or replaced. Among them was Asajj Ventress, a former Sith Assassin; Grievous was able to hold his own against Ventress in a standstill on Dathomir, even kicking her back until one of his arms was severed off as he fell to the ground, but in reaction, he had his droid open fire on her. One years later, Grievous would have another opportunity to fight Ventress again during her mission to assassinate her former master on Raxus; as they both tumbled down, Grievous landed over Ventress with his foot pressed against her throat, then grabbed her with all four hands, and hurled her to the lower level. However, she escaped. Earlier in that mission, Grievous fought Quinlan Vos, losing his lightsabers and hand at first, but eventually overpowering Vos in midair and pushing him back into the wall before being locked in a security center. Grievous also dueled the former Sith Lord Maul on two separate occasions, both resulting in stalemates.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' Aside from attacking someone else's lightsaber with his own, Grievous could also quickly deflect and block projectiles, such as blaster shots and [[booma]]s, with one or two lightsabers, much like a Jedi, and spinning either of them. In addition, he could throw his lightsaber by spinning his hand or throwing it directly at his opponent. ===Other abilities=== {{Quote|I met a Kaleesh on my travels who bragged of a revered warrior. He supposedly had cybernetic implants for enhanced combat!|An artist, in his journal|}} Grievous chose an unorthodox style while contending with the Jedi, using his four arms to his advantage. While having no Force ability, Grievous countered his lack of supernatural abilities with cybernetic upgrades: his artificial limbs and cybernetic systems allowed the reflexes and agility to equal those of the Jedi, making him dangerous to those he encountered. Grievous' keen senses and the precision of his mechanical arms and split armor allowed him to separate his two arms into four, making him capable of wielding four lightsabers at once with devastating effect. He could engage in lightsaber combat and use a blaster at close range at the same time, a lethal double threat for even an experienced, Force-sensitive opponent. [[File:EscapePlan-SWVPotDS.png|thumb|right|270px|Grievous could move very quickly when using all his limbs for locomotion.]] With his mechanical hands, whether divided into four or not, Grievous can spin lightsabers at a horrifying speed, turning them into devastating energy pinwheels. This became his preferred method, and some Jedi he encountered were quick enough to deflect it. He could also rotate his torso; when clones piled on top of him during the Battle of Saleucami, he used that ability to throw the troopers off him. His magnetic, claw-like limbs allowed him to cling, spider-like, to the outside panels of starships or quickly scale vertical metal surfaces, to easily climb walls and even ceilings to reach areas that would otherwise be difficult to access. Each arm can also function as a leg, and he employs his extra limbs to assist him in scurrying forward like a huge insect with spider-like agility. Grievous was capable of fighting fairly, but he was willing to do whatever it took and resort to any weapon or backup to win a fight, utilizing all of the technology at his disposal. When he locked blades with others, Grievous used one of his free arms to grab, toss, or draw out a blaster. He would also either use his IG-100 MagnaGuards to help him during his fight, or fight his opponent for him to wear them down long enough to personally deliver the final blow. Grievous was very fast as he was able to use his cybernetics to crawl on the ground and make a quick escape if he needed to. Not only was he fast, but he also had enhanced strength, With a single kick, Grievous was able to send someone across the corridor or atop a gunship, almost toppling it over, hurled a varactyl off of him, using only his hands and feet to crush the [[Mandalorian armor|Mandalorian's powerful armor]] and skulls, and delivered a single blow powerful enough to make a dent. His hand-to-hand combat abilities far exceeded those of an ordinary soldier, as he utilized his two or four arms fighting in a unique style, lifting, throwing, choking, and crushing with either just his bare hands or powerful durasteel feet that were magnetized and so sharp that they were effectively talons. Additionally, he could even transfer weapons with them into his hand. [[File:Grievous_Charred.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Equipped with strong armor, Grievous could stand up to explosions and other attacks.]] With a metal body stronger than any droid's shell, Grievous was very durable and could even resist explosions from fuel barrels. His biological remains were very much not fireproof, but they remained safe behind his armor. Thanks to his cyborg form, Grievous was able to survive in space and grip effectively onto a ship's hull. When Kenobi kicked at him during the Battle of Utapau, Grievous hardly felt it, but it very much hurt Kenobi. Unlike most opponents, the Kaleesh cyborg could afford to lose a limb or two during battle, seemingly unfazed by his injuries, which may slow him down but not stop him. However, damage and defeat forced him to return home for repairs and medical checks. With his powerful armored body, he has proven sufficient to withstand damage on numerous occasions,''[[Star Wars Annual 2016]]'' unharmed after being hit with a Force push hard enough to crack a ship's window, being slammed into a wall hard enough to cause a cloud of dust, or being tackled against a ship's window, but it seemed to have little effect on him. Grievous takes no harm when he crashes his speeder into a herd of varactyls or when he walks past through Mother Talzin's magick barrier, capable of absorbing blaster fire and Force lightning, with a Force lightning barrage by Sidious and Dooku. After being flung back with a Force push against the heavy machinery, hard enough to leave a large dent, and then plummeting down, despite losing two of his last remaining lightsabers, he was still able to escape. ===Military skills=== {{Quote|The general's description of your tactics have been one hundred percent accurate today. Very impressive, even by ''my'' standards.|TV-94, to Anakin Skywalker|}} [[File:GoH-Grievous.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous was a force to be reckoned with in both strategy and combat.]] On his homeworld, Grievous had previously demonstrated his talents and proven himself to be a brilliant military leader, training and leading his people expertly. That trait remained when he became a cyborg general in command of the Separatist Droid Army. Grievous was also a competent strategist as he used his massive army to overwhelm his opponents. Grievous recognized that clone troopers were superior than his droids. He had developed a method capable of defeating a Jedi and the clones under his command by deploying a mix of command droids and MagnaGuards. The Kaleesh cyborg utilized his strategic abilities to prioritize the pursuit of Jedi Generals, board their ships, and apprehend them. Grievous threaten the Jedi Council with such great threat that a team of their best Jedi were dispatched. Grievous sometimes enlisted [[Commerce Guild]] forces for combat on rocky worlds or in urban areas, while [[OG-9 homing spider droid|OC-9 homing spider droids]] served as heavy armor and siege weaponry, with modified [[Spelunker probe droid]]s providing reconnaissance and sabotage. Grievous led a devastating campaign in the Outer Rim, crushing multiple legions and fleets along the way. In the Battle of Bothawui, Grievous was able to lead his fleet through Bothawui's planetary ring, taking advantage of asteroids to defend himself from surprise attacks, and using this strategy allowed him to damage a Republic cruiser until Skywalker realized what he was up to. He was able to correctly anticipate the Republic's movements and accurately foresee Anakin's tactics during the Battle of Saleucami. Grievous was also able to fool the Republic forces during the Battle of Kamino with his ships taking heavy casualties, completely fooling even Anakin, but Obi-Wan Kenobi, his rival, was the only person who eventually identified his plan. Later, he led his fleets to victory against Kenobi's, the Republic's wise, tactical Jedi General, and took over his flagship without losing a single capital ship. He could calculate with certainty, based on previous experience, that the odds were stacked against them at the Battle of Zanbar. even on the verge of victory at Ord Mantell. He was also able to recognize that Maul had yet to deploy warships during the Battle on Ord Mantell. Tey-Zuka calculated that the enemy ships had been destroyed on the initial bombardment, but soon their [[Grievous's Providence-class Dreadnought (Campaign against the Shadow Collective)|dreadnought]] was hit, and Grievous recognized that they had been lured into a trap. He managed to lure Depa Billaba into a trap, cutting off her exits and surrounding her with droids on Mygeeto. He also had an advantage because he could directly command his battle droids with his two antennae built into his head and even access the system via [[comlink]]s built into his cybernetic systems, directing the ''Invisible Hand's'' defense. [[File:ImperviumPlating-SWZ.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous pilots the ''Soulless One''.]] The general gained a reputation as a talented flier and piloted a customized [[Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter|Belbullab-22 starfighter]] known as the ''Soulless One''. He was skilled enough to avoid and escape Anakin Skywalker's starfighter. Not only did Grievous successfully avoid each laser fire, but he also managed to achieve hyperspace without a single shot, demonstrating his superior cyborg-enhanced piloting skills. Although it should be noted that Anakin almost shot him down, but his starfighter lost a piece of shrapnel embedded in the fighter that caused it to careen off course. He managed to keep up with Skywalker, who was considered the best pilot in the Republic, scoring enough hits on the Jedi's [[Unidentified freighter (Utapau)|freighter]] to damage it. While he was an amazingly talented fighter on the ground, Grievous recognized that his skills as a fighter pilot, although not insignificant, were not comparable to those of a Jedi and preferred to abandon a battle.{{HelmetCollectionCite|5|Databank A-Z}} ==Equipment== {{Quote|So uncivilized…|Obi-Wan Kenobi disposing of Grievous's blaster|}} [[File:Annihilator_blaster_sw_thi_blaster.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous wielded a custom DT-57 "Annihilator."]] Despite not having Force sensitivity or official Jedi training, Grievous fought using a collection of stolen lightsabers. In contrast to his Jedi adversaries, and aside from an expanding collection of stolen lightsabers he utilized in hand-to-hand combat, he also owned a custom [[DT-57 "Annihilator" blaster|DT-57 "Annihilator"]] blaster pistol called the "Grievance Striker"{{Destiny|set=Convergence|cardname=Grievance Striker|link=https://swdestinydb.com/card/09169}} in range combat and uses any weapon, such as an electrostaff or other models of blaster, such as the [[DC-17]] pistol or E-5 rifle. Grievous was equipped with grapple lines built into his wrists, which he could launch at a long distance to attach himself to objects. The general also piloted a customized Belbullab-22 starfighter known as the ''Soulless One''. Not only did he use his own starfighter, but the brutal cyborg used other vehicles, including a combat speeder and a modified wheel bike. ==Behind the scenes== ===Overview=== {{Quote|With General Grievous, I wanted somebody who was reminiscent of what Anakin is going to become, which is a half man, half robot. While Grievous would only have around six minutes of screen time in the final film, with Darth Sidious actually being the film's primary antagonist, StarWars.com had teased Grievous's coming role in ''Revenge of the Sith'' on [[May 26]], 2004, claiming that Grievous would be "the Villain of Episode III."{{SWArchive|url=kids/explore/episode-iii/news20040526.html|text=The Villain of Episode III}} In ''Revenge of the Sith'', the character was portrayed by [[Matthew Wood]], the film's supervising sound editor. In his first appearance in Chapter 20, Grievous had been voiced by [[John DiMaggio]] before [[Richard McGonagle]] took on the role for the rest of the original ''Clone Wars'' series.{{CW|21}} However, StarWars.com had confirmed before release of ''Revenge of the Sith'' that Grievous "[wouldn't] necessarily" sound in the film like he did in that animated series. Since ''Revenge of the Sith'', Wood has retained the role of Grievous, portraying the droid general in the [[2008]] animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' and numerous other post-''Revenge of the Sith'' appearances. ===Development=== ====Creation==== {{Quote|It's rare to have a new main character that has to be designed from scratch.|Warren Fu|{{InsiderCite|213|Warren Fu: Envisaging Grievous}}}} [[File:Head_of_the_Confederacy.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Early concept art of Grievous.]] During the development of ''Revenge of the Sith'', Grievous was created when it was clear that, with Dooku dying early in the film, the movie would need a new villain.{{SW|url=news/10-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-archives-1999-2005|text=10 Things We Learned from ''The Star Wars Archives 1999-2005''}} The initial instructions that Director George Lucas gave the Art Department were very open-ended: "a droid general," specifying that the character needed to be reminiscent of the [[Original trilogy]]'s Darth Vader without being a copy of the famous Sith Lord.{{SW|url=news/10-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-archives-1999-2005|text=10 Things We Learned from ''The Star Wars Archives 1999-2005''}} From that vague direction, the artists developed a lot of explorations, some purely mechanical, some not, for the look of General Grievous. Lucas later noted to the crew that Grievous needed to clearly and visually be a cyborg, denying early designs that depicted his mask with robotic [[photoreceptor]]s. An early concept design featured Grievous as "a disembodied alien head, trailing a number of prehensile tentacles".{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/artofrev/2005/02/artofrev20050207.html|series=Art of Revenge|text=Head of the Separatists}} Legend has it that Nilo Rodis-Jamero got the idea for Boba Fett's ship from the San Rafael streetlamps. In that spirit, concept artist [[Warren Fu]] drew on unexpected ideas from everyday objects. A spray bottle inspired his first passes at interesting heads. Those designs weren't picked, but George gravitated towards another one of Wu's designs, which ended up being the MagnaGuards.{{InsiderCite|213|Warren Fu: Envisaging Grievous}} Amongst the artists of the Episode III art department who made designs for Grievous were [[Derek Thompson]], [[Erik Tiemens]], [[Alex Jaeger]], and [[Warren Fu]]. Ultimately, it was a sketch by the latter that most defined what Grievous would look like, even though it was only a quick sketch that he was not very impressed by. Lucas, meanwhile, was instantly impressed by the drawing. [[File:RockDrillStatue.png|thumb|left|300px|Jacob Epstein's statue ''Rock Drill'' (reconstruction pictured) has been connected to Grievous's design by commentators.]] According to StarWars.com, artists [[Robert E. Barnes|Robert Barnes]], [[Iain McCaig]], and [[Ryan Church]] were also involved in creating Grievous. When interviewed ''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]'', Wu stated Grievous's white coloration was created to be the opposite of Darth Vader's black suit, further noting that, within Chinese culture, the color of white represents death. According to [[Rob Coleman]], [[Wikipedia:Ray Harryhausen|Ray Harryhausen]]’s [[Wikipedia:Kali|Kali]] from the [[Wikipedia:The Golden Voyage of Sinbad|''The Golden Voyage of Sinbad'']] was an inspiration for the four-armed general.{{Twitter|ArfKeldo|status/1065365045045952512|[[Rob Coleman]]|quote=Yes, Ray Harryhausen’s Kali from the Golden Voyage of Sinbad (1973) was definitely an inspiration for the four armed General Grievous|archivedate=20240801022401}} From Warren Fu's initial sketch came further refinements, and the finalized character would emerge from discussions between Barnes, McCaig, Church, and Wu, followed by sketches. Finally a foot-tall maquette sculpted by Robert Barnes showed what the general would look like in three dimensions. This sculpture was further modified to become a realistic computer-generated model for use by [[Industrial Light & Magic]]. According to [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (TV series)|''The Clone Wars'']] and [[Star Wars Rebels|''Rebels'']] co-producer and writer, [[Henry Gilroy]], Lucas briefly considered having [[Maul]] be Grievous, in that his upper half would be inside the armor.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'', Disc 7, Star Wars Archives: Episode III General Grievous Marquette description Commentators have drawn a connection between Grievous's design and ''[[Wikipedia:Rock Drill (Jacob Epstein)|Rock Drill]]'',{{BookCite|author=Brandon, Laura|title=Art and War|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing|date=2012-11-25|isbn=9780857732811}} a 1913-1915{{WebCite|url=https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/robotic-futures-epsteins-rock-drill-1913-15|text=Robotic Futures Epstein’s Rock Drill 1913-15|archivedate=20250419013530}} statue by British artist [[Wikipedia:Jacob Epstein|Jacob Epstein]]. The statue's design has also been compared to the B1 battle droid.{{BookCite|author=Mullins, Charlotte|title=A Little History of Art|publisher=Yale University Press|date=2022-04-26|pages=234|isbn=9780300265538}} After Lucas approved the maquette design, Industrial Light & Magic began its work on creating the character's CGI model. The model of Grievous was one of the most complicated ILM had ever constructed, having so many parts of differing physical qualities. ====Continued production and filming==== On set, no one person played Grievous, though off-screen dialogue reader [[Duncan Young]] read his lines. For combat sequences, stunt performer [[Kyle Rowling]] wore a greenscreen or bluescreen suit to play Grievous in his battles with Obi-Wan Kenobi. During production, the crew found it hard to film the duel between Kenobi and Grievous when the cyborg warlord uses all four of his hands. After considering having one actor sit atop another or having one suspended from the ceiling to achieve the tall general's multiple armed attack run, it was decided to use two stunt performers, with one standing in front of the other, to achieve the scene, but it was decided this strategy did not work out. Their next idea was to have one performer learn both Grievous's above and below attacks, allowing the complete attack run to be assembled out of both passes in post-production. In the end, it was decided that Grievous should lose several of his hands quickly to make filming easier on the crew, explaining why Grievous only briefly uses all four of his limbs to duel in ''Revenge of the Sith''.''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]'' Lucas originally wanted a powerful erect posture for the 'droid, but decided during production to have him rendered hunched and sickly.[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|''Entertainment Weekly #820'']] To that end, during the production of ''Revenge of the Sith'', George Lucas came into work one day with a cough and decided that it would be amusing to record it and use it on the new Episode III villain. According to animation director [[Rob Coleman]], the idea of this sicky element was to foreshadow ''Star Wars''{{'}} more famous half-man/half-machine, Vader, whom Grievous was "like the alpha version of." Grievous's vampiric movements were inspired by the German horror classic [[Wikipedia:Nosferatu|''Nosferatu'']], one of many monster-movie references in ''Sith''. Coleman further stated in the ''Revenge of the Sith'' DVD commentary that Grievous's cybernetics were seen as a step in the development of the Vader armor by Lucas and company, with Vader's cybernetics finally perfecting what had been the prototype with Grievous. This explains why Grievous suffers from a cough but Vader does not. [[File:ROTS-GeneralGrievousheadshot.png|thumb|right|300px|General Grievous's computer generated design was approved in March 2004 but would not be completed for some time (Grievous's finalized model in ''Revenge of the Sith'', pictured).]] At least as argued by some fan and commentators,{{WebCite|url=https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/general-grievous-clone-wars-20-year-anniversary|text=20 Years Ago, Star Wars Introduced its Most Hardcore Villain — Then Ruined Him|author=Ryan Britt|date=2024-04-09|work=Inverse|archivedate=20250124112115}} there is a difference between the more "relentless" Grievous seen in pre-''Revenge of the Sith'' material and the quick-to-retreat, "mustache-twirling" villain depicted in the film, an apparent contradiction even acknowledged by [[Star Wars Insider|''Star Wars'' Insider]]. It was George Lucas who wanted to make Grievous more of a "Dracula Droid" and made the call after watching a rough cut of ''Revenge of the Sith''.{{InsiderCite|149|General Grievous: Beneath the Armor}} Grievous's computer generated design was approved in March of 2004. According to StarWars.com, as of May 26 of that year, Grievous's model had yet to "painted," nor had his body language and animation been refined or developed. As such, Grievous's model had not yet been added to the cut of the film as it existed at that time. No voice actor had been found at that time as well, with producer [[Rick McCallum]] hypothesizing that voice-work for Grievous and the rest of the cast would begin sometime between August and November of that year. ====Finding a voice==== It would be many months before a voice actor was hired to perform Grievous's dialogue. In the end, Supervising Sound Editor Matthew Wood had submitted the winning audition. According to Wood himself, he was a sound editor for Lucas's projects when Lucas started recording many different actors for the voice of Grievous. They had planned to process Grievous's voice to make it sound like it was coming out of his "little cyborg face."{{YouTube|video=D9sSSJ-h4hQ|text=Matthew Wood interview Voice of general grievous|channel=@Ecwa2k|name=ECWA}} Lucasfilm recorded [[Ben Burtt]]'s voice for General Grievous while [[Rick McCallum]] put out a huge casting call. [[Chris Scarabosio]], the dialogue editor, and Wood devised how Grievous was supposed to sound, and George approved it.{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/04/matt-wood-interview-general-grievous.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Matt Wood interview General Grievous Star Wars|date=2005-09}} After getting auditions from various actors, Lucas never gravitated towards one he liked. Wood had the luxury of hearing everyone's auditions, so his friend encouraged him to put one. Chris said Matthew should try to get the part, but he thought it was "too weird and I couldn't do it." In his own words, Wood had an advantage in knowing what George wanted as he heard him talk to the actors about Grievous. Finally, Wood decided to give it a try. Chris recorded him and put the tape under an anonymous name with the rest. Matthew didn't think about it after that until one day Rick McCallum came up to him and asked if Matthew had the agent's name of the person whose voice was on a certain tape since he had all the documentation. Wood thought it was a prank, "that he knew it was me and I had screwed up," but Rick couldn't have known. Thinking he had crossed the line, Wood confessed it was him. McCallum apparently said afterward, "Are you s**tting me?" before asking Wood what to do, to which he suggested telling George. McCallum then called George and said it was Matthew Wood's voice. George then called Wood and asked him to come over and record it. Wood would later state that Lucas was "really cool about it," much to his own shock of receiving the role of a lead villain in a new Star Wars movie. He would later say of the experience in an interview, "It was fun, because I don't have any shyness around George." By Wood's own admission, that chance changed his life and opened the doors for many other voice-acting roles. When auditioning, Matthew Wood used an Eastern European accent from recently spending time in Prague and a [[Wikipedia:Bela Lugosi|Bela Lugosi]] Dracula component that Lucas himself liked, mixed with "a little bit of a drill sergeant vibe." According to Mathew Wood, Grievous's original origin was that he was a Jedi who had been betrayed by Dooku and "had a bone to pick with the Jedi." Wood didn't tell anyone about his role until, finally, when the film was printed, he told "everybody." Before Matthew Wood was cast as Grievous, British actor [[Gary Oldman]] was offered Grievous's role. According to a report in the [[Wikipedia:Daily Star (United Kingdom)|Daily Star]], which quoted Oldman's official spokesman, "Gary was excited and looking forward to working on the film. The snag is that the movie is being made without members of the [[Wikipedia:Screen Actors Guild|Screen Actors Guild]]. It means Gary would have been working illegally overseas. Out of respect and solidarity with the other members, he could not and would not consider violating the rules of his union." Production had already been completed, and Oldman's work was limited to providing the voice of General Grievous - described at the time as an evil Jedi Knight killer - and was due to be completed during the post-production process taking place then at the LucasFilm HQ, [[Skywalker Ranch]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2004/sep/16/news.starwars|text=Oldman shelves Star Wars role in the name of thespian union|date=2004-09-16|work=The Guardian|archivedate=20140916201231}} Gary Oldman said he did a voice on the ''Happy Sad Confused'' podcast. However, due to something to do with union and non-union talent, he did not want to be at the center of any controversy surrounding breaking union rules. He praised director George Lucas, stating, "[Lucas] directed me the whole thing; yeah, he was terrific."{{WebCite|url=https://teletraan.libsyn.com/42c52f07f4e073d169ea793ff34e8065__1ba59e84de3cd4900654ea5eba0faca06e4bc0f161ebc188495379994f7d2b38__12z/p/3/f/5/3f52fcd3fdfeda93/Gary_Oldman.mp3?rpid=00c7600041f5c639ae078170c31a0e8e__d8c388eecc712fda307ba6a880d1b437f8d62e3da2e3195d70733db0ad4a57c5&c_id=154495896&cs_id=154495896&Expires=1722975619&Signature=cpvHua7aKJmR9STnsFQkWOD6qdDNVdyFamgOFwJcyBSlIEKoMvDo5ty7ui2BeykOIkMeCZB0cHscibG~GR9cQHw2oCpGVqGEECVjY8zZhAiaO3JLylPo1UqR1dEavIFZuX9~HD5UmfgX5ayG9SBtsRa550WBqrjhJZXJ2~jYLXthDZsf31NJzCVmbEDpHt-6r5PxF5yk50UHx9UisfAlawqHdlFxxn6JvvCyrko~iY2BM5yEWbJFRNBKB3h1LXBKTDWqg9ep~-rR3pUqXqynVgEp5n3Z7xiCOcP22IwwXWPdKAy7EtOKZ61~qbb-1KYFgurmbe2ad9c~a4jxQovKLw__&Key-Pair-Id=K1YS7LZGUP96OI|text=Happy Sad Confused: Gary Oldman|date=2022-06-08|work=Happy Sad Confused podcast|archivedate=20240805202052}} ===''LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales''=== In the non-canon series ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales]]'' episodes "[[Exit from Endor]]"{{Droid Tales|Exit from Endor}} credits and "[[Crisis on Coruscant]]," Grievous was voiced by [[Kirby Morrow]].{{Droid Tales|Crisis on Coruscant}} credits ===Concept art galleries=== {{Gallery |source=''[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith]]'' |storyboards= |concept= Conceptscourge.jpg|Early concept production art of Grievous. As such, the three began conspiring to destroy Grievous and rebuild him into a super-cyborg of servitude.{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=San Hill - Banking Clan Chairman}} At the time, [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] said this was an outdated Legends reference{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/672253588018618368|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Tweet lost but did state that San Hill - Banking Clan Chairman - ''Base Series 1'' contains an outdated reference to Legends via San Hill, Poggle, and Dooku working together to destroy and rebuild Grievous.|nobackup=1}} based on the character's backstory from the comic "[[The Eyes of Revolution]]."{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}} However, as other modern sources have canonized "The Eyes of Revolution"-inspired details, the Story Group may have changed its mind. "[[The Duel for Peace]]" states that Kenobi had not seen Grievous in a long time before the Battle of Utapau. However, they had last seen each other face-to-face in the Battle of Coruscant mere days prior. [[Star Wars Bust Collection 68|''Star Wars Bust Collection'' 68]] also claimed that Grievous hid on Utapau in "the closing weeks" of the war after the Battle of Coruscant.{{BustCollectionCite|68|Character}} However, as only a few days pass between the Battles of Coruscant and Utapau, that cannot be accurate. The [[2023]] reference magazine [[Star Wars Starships & Vehicles 55|''Star Wars Starships & Vehicles'' 55]] states that Grievous requested a more advanced battle droid after becoming Supreme Commander of the Separatists, which led to the development of the MagnaGuard. In specific, it claims he asked for more advanced droids than the [[Trade Federation]]'s simple combat droids, which he criticized for relying on commands from a central [[computer]] and being incapable of learning from their mistakes on their own. The majority of sources, however, state that Grievous requested such droids back when he was fighting for the InterGalactic Banking Clan, placing the creation of the MagnaGuards earlier in the ''Star Wars'' timeline. This article sides with the majority of sources and states that Grievous requested his advanced droid troops during his days as an IGBC enforcer.
